  sup_le (sdiff_le_iff.2 ha) <| sdiff_le_iff.2 hb

theorem symmDiff_le_iff {a b c : α} : a ∆ b ≤ c ↔ a ≤ b ⊔ c ∧ b ≤ a ⊔ c := by
  simp_rw [symmDiff, sup_le_iff, sdiff_le_iff]

@[simp]
theorem symmDiff_le_sup {a b : α} : a ∆ b ≤ a ⊔ b :=
  sup_le_sup sdiff_le sdiff_le

theorem symmDiff_eq_sup_sdiff_inf : a ∆ b = (a ⊔ b) \ (a ⊓ b) := by simp [sup_sdiff, symmDiff]

theorem Disjoint.symmDiff_eq_sup {a b : α} (h : Disjoint a b) : a ∆ b = a ⊔ b := by
  rw [symmDiff, h.sdiff_eq_left, h.sdiff_eq_right]

theorem symmDiff_sdiff : a ∆ b \ c = a \ (b ⊔ c) ⊔ b \ (a ⊔ c) := by
  rw [symmDiff, sup_sdiff_distrib, sdiff_sdiff_left, sdiff_sdiff_left]

theorem symmDiff_sdiff_inf : a ∆ b \ (a ⊓ b) = a ∆ b := by

  simp [symmDiff]

theorem symmDiff_sdiff_eq_sup : a ∆ (b \ a) = a ⊔ b := by
  rw [symmDiff, sdiff_idem]
  exact
    le_antisymm (sup_le_sup sdiff_le sdiff_le)
      (sup_le le_sdiff_sup <| le_sdiff_sup.trans <| sup_le le_sup_right le_sdiff_sup)

@[simp]
theorem sdiff_symmDiff_eq_sup : (a \ b) ∆ b = a ⊔ b := by
  rw [symmDiff_comm, symmDiff_sdiff_eq_sup, sup_comm]

@[simp]
theorem symmDiff_sup_inf : a ∆ b ⊔ a ⊓ b = a ⊔ b := by
  refine le_antisymm (sup_le symmDiff_le_sup inf_le_sup) ?_
  rw [sup_inf_left, symmDiff]
  refine sup_le (le_inf le_sup_right ?_) (le_inf ?_ le_sup_right)
  · rw [sup_right_comm]
    exact le_sup_of_le_left le_sdiff_sup
  · rw [sup_assoc]
    exact le_sup_of_le_right le_sdiff_sup

@[simp]

theorem symmDiff_symmDiff_inf : a ∆ b ∆ (a ⊓ b) = a ⊔ b := by
  rw [← symmDiff_sdiff_inf a, sdiff_symmDiff_eq_sup, symmDiff_sup_inf]

theorem inf_symmDiff_symmDiff : (a ⊓ b) ∆ (a ∆ b) = a ⊔ b := by
  rw [symmDiff_comm, symmDiff_symmDiff_inf]

theorem symmDiff_triangle : a ∆ c ≤ a ∆ b ⊔ b ∆ c := by
  refine (sup_le_sup (sdiff_triangle a b c) <| sdiff_triangle _ b _).trans_eq ?_
  rw [sup_comm (c \ b), sup_sup_sup_comm, symmDiff, symmDiff]

theorem le_symmDiff_sup_right (a b : α) : a ≤ (a ∆ b) ⊔ b := by
  convert symmDiff_triangle a b ⊥ <;> rw [symmDiff_bot]

theorem le_symmDiff_sup_left (a b : α) : b ≤ (a ∆ b) ⊔ a :=
  symmDiff_comm a b ▸ le_symmDiff_sup_right ..

  calc
    a ∆ b ∆ c = a ∆ b \ c ⊔ c \ a ∆ b := symmDiff_def _ _
    _ = a \ (b ⊔ c) ⊔ b \ (a ⊔ c) ⊔ (c \ (a ⊔ b) ⊔ c ⊓ a ⊓ b) := by

import Mathlib.Order.BooleanAlgebra

/-!
# Symmetric difference and bi-implication

This file defines the symmetric difference and bi-implication operators in (co-)Heyting algebras.

## Examples

Some examples are
* The symmetric difference of two sets is the set of elements that are in either but not both.
* The symmetric difference on propositions is `Xor'`.
* The symmetric difference on `Bool` is `Bool.xor`.
* The equivalence of propositions. Two propositions are equivalent if they imply each other.
* The symmetric difference translates to addition when considering a Boolean algebra as a Boolean
  ring.

## Main declarations

* `symmDiff`: The symmetric difference operator, defined as `(a \ b) ⊔ (b \ a)`
* `bihimp`: The bi-implication operator, defined as `(b ⇨ a) ⊓ (a ⇨ b)`

In generalized Boolean algebras, the symmetric difference operator is:

* `symmDiff_comm`: commutative, and
* `symmDiff_assoc`: associative.

## Notations

* `a ∆ b`: `symmDiff a b`
* `a ⇔ b`: `bihimp a b`

## References

The proof of associativity follows the note "Associativity of the Symmetric Difference of Sets: A
Proof from the Book" by John McCuan:

* <https://people.math.gatech.edu/~mccuan/courses/4317/symmetricdifference.pdf>

## Tags

boolean ring, generalized boolean algebra, boolean algebra, symmetric difference, bi-implication,
Heyting
-/

assert_not_exists RelIso

open Function OrderDual

variable {ι α β : Type*} {π : ι → Type*}

/-- The symmetric difference operator on a type with `⊔` and `\` is `(A \ B) ⊔ (B \ A)`. -/
def symmDiff [Max α] [SDiff α] (a b : α) : α :=
  a \ b ⊔ b \ a

/-- The Heyting bi-implication is `(b ⇨ a) ⊓ (a ⇨ b)`. This generalizes equivalence of
propositions. -/
def bihimp [Min α] [HImp α] (a b : α) : α :=
  (b ⇨ a) ⊓ (a ⇨ b)

/-- Notation for symmDiff -/
scoped[symmDiff] infixl:100 " ∆ " => symmDiff

/-- Notation for bihimp -/
scoped[symmDiff] infixl:100 " ⇔ " => bihimp

open scoped symmDiff

theorem symmDiff_def [Max α] [SDiff α] (a b : α) : a ∆ b = a \ b ⊔ b \ a :=
  rfl

theorem bihimp_def [Min α] [HImp α] (a b : α) : a ⇔ b = (b ⇨ a) ⊓ (a ⇨ b) :=
  rfl

theorem symmDiff_eq_Xor' (p q : Prop) : p ∆ q = Xor' p q :=
  rfl

  iff_iff_implies_and_implies.symm.trans Iff.comm

theorem Bool.symmDiff_eq_xor : ∀ p q : Bool, p ∆ q = xor p q := by decide

  rw [symmDiff_comm, symmDiff_sdiff_eq_sup, sup_comm]

  refine le_antisymm (sup_le symmDiff_le_sup inf_le_sup) ?_
  rw [sup_inf_left, symmDiff]
  refine sup_le (le_inf le_sup_right ?_) (le_inf ?_ le_sup_right)
  · rw [sup_right_comm]
    exact le_sup_of_le_left le_sdiff_sup
  · rw [sup_assoc]
    exact le_sup_of_le_right le_sdiff_sup

  refine (sup_le_sup (sdiff_triangle a b c) <| sdiff_triangle _ b _).trans_eq ?_
  rw [sup_comm (c \ b), sup_sup_sup_comm, symmDiff, symmDiff]

theorem le_symmDiff_sup_right (a b : α) : a ≤ (a ∆ b) ⊔ b := by
  convert symmDiff_triangle a b ⊥ <;> rw [symmDiff_bot]

theorem le_symmDiff_sup_left (a b : α) : b ≤ (a ∆ b) ⊔ a :=
  symmDiff_comm a b ▸ le_symmDiff_sup_right ..

  calc
    a ∆ b ∆ c = a ∆ b \ c ⊔ c \ a ∆ b := symmDiff_def _ _

import Mathlib.Order.BooleanAlgebra

/-!
# Symmetric difference and bi-implication

This file defines the symmetric difference and bi-implication operators in (co-)Heyting algebras.

## Examples

Some examples are
* The symmetric difference of two sets is the set of elements that are in either but not both.
* The symmetric difference on propositions is `Xor'`.
* The symmetric difference on `Bool` is `Bool.xor`.
* The equivalence of propositions. Two propositions are equivalent if they imply each other.
* The symmetric difference translates to addition when considering a Boolean algebra as a Boolean
  ring.

## Main declarations

* `symmDiff`: The symmetric difference operator, defined as `(a \ b) ⊔ (b \ a)`
* `bihimp`: The bi-implication operator, defined as `(b ⇨ a) ⊓ (a ⇨ b)`

In generalized Boolean algebras, the symmetric difference operator is:

* `symmDiff_comm`: commutative, and
* `symmDiff_assoc`: associative.

## Notations

* `a ∆ b`: `symmDiff a b`
* `a ⇔ b`: `bihimp a b`

## References

The proof of associativity follows the note "Associativity of the Symmetric Difference of Sets: A
Proof from the Book" by John McCuan:

* <https://people.math.gatech.edu/~mccuan/courses/4317/symmetricdifference.pdf>

## Tags

boolean ring, generalized boolean algebra, boolean algebra, symmetric difference, bi-implication,
Heyting
-/

open Function OrderDual

variable {ι α β : Type*} {π : ι → Type*}

/-- The symmetric difference operator on a type with `⊔` and `\` is `(A \ B) ⊔ (B \ A)`. -/
def symmDiff [Max α] [SDiff α] (a b : α) : α :=
  a \ b ⊔ b \ a

/-- The Heyting bi-implication is `(b ⇨ a) ⊓ (a ⇨ b)`. This generalizes equivalence of
propositions. -/
def bihimp [Min α] [HImp α] (a b : α) : α :=
  (b ⇨ a) ⊓ (a ⇨ b)

/-- Notation for symmDiff -/
scoped[symmDiff] infixl:100 " ∆ " => symmDiff

/-- Notation for bihimp -/
scoped[symmDiff] infixl:100 " ⇔ " => bihimp

open scoped symmDiff

theorem symmDiff_def [Max α] [SDiff α] (a b : α) : a ∆ b = a \ b ⊔ b \ a :=
  rfl

theorem bihimp_def [Min α] [HImp α] (a b : α) : a ⇔ b = (b ⇨ a) ⊓ (a ⇨ b) :=
  rfl

theorem symmDiff_eq_Xor' (p q : Prop) : p ∆ q = Xor' p q :=
  rfl

  iff_iff_implies_and_implies.symm.trans Iff.comm

theorem Bool.symmDiff_eq_xor : ∀ p q : Bool, p ∆ q = xor p q := by decide

  sup_le_sup sdiff_le sdiff_le

  rw [symmDiff_comm, symmDiff_sdiff_eq_sup, sup_comm]

  refine le_antisymm (sup_le symmDiff_le_sup inf_le_sup) ?_
  rw [sup_inf_left, symmDiff]
  refine sup_le (le_inf le_sup_right ?_) (le_inf ?_ le_sup_right)
  · rw [sup_right_comm]
    exact le_sup_of_le_left le_sdiff_sup
  · rw [sup_assoc]
    exact le_sup_of_le_right le_sdiff_sup

theorem le_symmDiff_sup_right (a b : α) : a ≤ (a ∆ b) ⊔ b := by
  convert symmDiff_triangle a b ⊥ <;> rw [symmDiff_bot]

theorem le_symmDiff_sup_left (a b : α) : b ≤ (a ∆ b) ⊔ a :=
  symmDiff_comm a b ▸ le_symmDiff_sup_right ..

theorem symmDiff_symmDiff_left :
    a ∆ b ∆ c = a \ (b ⊔ c) ⊔ b \ (a ⊔ c) ⊔ c \ (a ⊔ b) ⊔ a ⊓ b ⊓ c :=
  calc
    a ∆ b ∆ c = a ∆ b \ c ⊔ c \ a ∆ b := symmDiff_def _ _
    _ = a \ (b ⊔ c) ⊔ b \ (a ⊔ c) ⊔ (c \ (a ⊔ b) ⊔ c ⊓ a ⊓ b) := by

    a ∆ (b ∆ c) = a \ (b ⊔ c) ⊔ b \ (a ⊔ c) ⊔ c \ (a ⊔ b) ⊔ a ⊓ b ⊓ c :=

import Mathlib.Order.BooleanAlgebra

import Mathlib.Logic.Equiv.Basic

/-!
# Symmetric difference and bi-implication

This file defines the symmetric difference and bi-implication operators in (co-)Heyting algebras.

## Examples

Some examples are
* The symmetric difference of two sets is the set of elements that are in either but not both.
* The symmetric difference on propositions is `Xor'`.
* The symmetric difference on `Bool` is `Bool.xor`.
* The equivalence of propositions. Two propositions are equivalent if they imply each other.
* The symmetric difference translates to addition when considering a Boolean algebra as a Boolean
  ring.

## Main declarations

* `symmDiff`: The symmetric difference operator, defined as `(a \ b) ⊔ (b \ a)`
* `bihimp`: The bi-implication operator, defined as `(b ⇨ a) ⊓ (a ⇨ b)`

In generalized Boolean algebras, the symmetric difference operator is:

* `symmDiff_comm`: commutative, and
* `symmDiff_assoc`: associative.

## Notations

* `a ∆ b`: `symmDiff a b`
* `a ⇔ b`: `bihimp a b`

## References

The proof of associativity follows the note "Associativity of the Symmetric Difference of Sets: A
Proof from the Book" by John McCuan:

* <https://people.math.gatech.edu/~mccuan/courses/4317/symmetricdifference.pdf>

## Tags

boolean ring, generalized boolean algebra, boolean algebra, symmetric difference, bi-implication,
Heyting
-/

assert_not_exists RelIso

open Function OrderDual

variable {ι α β : Type*} {π : ι → Type*}

/-- The symmetric difference operator on a type with `⊔` and `\` is `(A \ B) ⊔ (B \ A)`. -/
def symmDiff [Max α] [SDiff α] (a b : α) : α :=
  a \ b ⊔ b \ a

/-- The Heyting bi-implication is `(b ⇨ a) ⊓ (a ⇨ b)`. This generalizes equivalence of
propositions. -/
def bihimp [Min α] [HImp α] (a b : α) : α :=
  (b ⇨ a) ⊓ (a ⇨ b)

/-- Notation for symmDiff -/
scoped[symmDiff] infixl:100 " ∆ " => symmDiff

/-- Notation for bihimp -/
scoped[symmDiff] infixl:100 " ⇔ " => bihimp

open scoped symmDiff

theorem symmDiff_def [Max α] [SDiff α] (a b : α) : a ∆ b = a \ b ⊔ b \ a :=
  rfl

theorem bihimp_def [Min α] [HImp α] (a b : α) : a ⇔ b = (b ⇨ a) ⊓ (a ⇨ b) :=
  rfl

theorem symmDiff_eq_Xor' (p q : Prop) : p ∆ q = Xor' p q :=
  rfl

@[simp]
theorem bihimp_iff_iff {p q : Prop} : p ⇔ q ↔ (p ↔ q) :=
  iff_iff_implies_and_implies.symm.trans Iff.comm

@[simp]
theorem Bool.symmDiff_eq_xor : ∀ p q : Bool, p ∆ q = xor p q := by decide

  sup_le (sdiff_le_iff.2 ha) <| sdiff_le_iff.2 hb

theorem symmDiff_le_iff {a b c : α} : a ∆ b ≤ c ↔ a ≤ b ⊔ c ∧ b ≤ a ⊔ c := by
  simp_rw [symmDiff, sup_le_iff, sdiff_le_iff]

@[simp]
theorem symmDiff_le_sup {a b : α} : a ∆ b ≤ a ⊔ b :=
  sup_le_sup sdiff_le sdiff_le

theorem symmDiff_eq_sup_sdiff_inf : a ∆ b = (a ⊔ b) \ (a ⊓ b) := by simp [sup_sdiff, symmDiff]

  rw [symmDiff, h.sdiff_eq_left, h.sdiff_eq_right]

theorem symmDiff_sdiff : a ∆ b \ c = a \ (b ⊔ c) ⊔ b \ (a ⊔ c) := by
  rw [symmDiff, sup_sdiff_distrib, sdiff_sdiff_left, sdiff_sdiff_left]

      (sup_le le_sdiff_sup <| le_sdiff_sup.trans <| sup_le le_sup_right le_sdiff_sup)

@[simp]

  rw [symmDiff_comm, symmDiff_sdiff_eq_sup, sup_comm]

@[simp]
theorem symmDiff_sup_inf : a ∆ b ⊔ a ⊓ b = a ⊔ b := by
  refine le_antisymm (sup_le symmDiff_le_sup inf_le_sup) ?_
  rw [sup_inf_left, symmDiff]
  refine sup_le (le_inf le_sup_right ?_) (le_inf ?_ le_sup_right)
  · rw [sup_right_comm]
    exact le_sup_of_le_left le_sdiff_sup
  · rw [sup_assoc]
    exact le_sup_of_le_right le_sdiff_sup

  rw [← symmDiff_sdiff_inf a, sdiff_symmDiff_eq_sup, symmDiff_sup_inf]

theorem symmDiff_triangle : a ∆ c ≤ a ∆ b ⊔ b ∆ c := by
  refine (sup_le_sup (sdiff_triangle a b c) <| sdiff_triangle _ b _).trans_eq ?_
  rw [sup_comm (c \ b), sup_sup_sup_comm, symmDiff, symmDiff]

theorem le_symmDiff_sup_right (a b : α) : a ≤ (a ∆ b) ⊔ b := by
  convert symmDiff_triangle a b ⊥ <;> rw [symmDiff_bot]

theorem le_symmDiff_sup_left (a b : α) : b ≤ (a ∆ b) ⊔ a :=
  symmDiff_comm a b ▸ le_symmDiff_sup_right ..

    _ = a \ (b ⊔ c) ⊔ b \ (a ⊔ c) ⊔ (c \ (a ⊔ b) ⊔ c ⊓ a ⊓ b) := by

    _ = a \ (b ⊔ c) ⊔ b \ (a ⊔ c) ⊔ c \ (a ⊔ b) ⊔ a ⊓ b ⊓ c := by ac_rfl

    a ∆ (b ∆ c) = a \ (b ⊔ c) ⊔ b \ (a ⊔ c) ⊔ c \ (a ⊔ b) ⊔ a ⊓ b ⊓ c :=
  calc
    a ∆ (b ∆ c) = a \ b ∆ c ⊔ b ∆ c \ a := symmDiff_def _ _
    _ = a \ (b ⊔ c) ⊔ a ⊓ b ⊓ c ⊔ (b \ (c ⊔ a) ⊔ c \ (b ⊔ a)) := by
        { rw [sdiff_symmDiff', sup_comm (a ⊓ b ⊓ c), symmDiff_sdiff] }
    _ = a \ (b ⊔ c) ⊔ b \ (a ⊔ c) ⊔ c \ (a ⊔ b) ⊔ a ⊓ b ⊓ c := by ac_rfl

import Mathlib.Order.BooleanAlgebra

import Mathlib.Logic.Equiv.Basic

/-!
# Symmetric difference and bi-implication

This file defines the symmetric difference and bi-implication operators in (co-)Heyting algebras.

## Examples

Some examples are
* The symmetric difference of two sets is the set of elements that are in either but not both.
* The symmetric difference on propositions is `Xor'`.
* The symmetric difference on `Bool` is `Bool.xor`.
* The equivalence of propositions. Two propositions are equivalent if they imply each other.
* The symmetric difference translates to addition when considering a Boolean algebra as a Boolean
  ring.

## Main declarations

* `symmDiff`: The symmetric difference operator, defined as `(a \ b) ⊔ (b \ a)`
* `bihimp`: The bi-implication operator, defined as `(b ⇨ a) ⊓ (a ⇨ b)`

In generalized Boolean algebras, the symmetric difference operator is:

* `symmDiff_comm`: commutative, and
* `symmDiff_assoc`: associative.

## Notations

* `a ∆ b`: `symmDiff a b`
* `a ⇔ b`: `bihimp a b`

## References

The proof of associativity follows the note "Associativity of the Symmetric Difference of Sets: A
Proof from the Book" by John McCuan:

* <https://people.math.gatech.edu/~mccuan/courses/4317/symmetricdifference.pdf>

## Tags

boolean ring, generalized boolean algebra, boolean algebra, symmetric difference, bi-implication,
Heyting
-/

assert_not_exists RelIso

open Function OrderDual

variable {ι α β : Type*} {π : ι → Type*}

/-- The symmetric difference operator on a type with `⊔` and `\` is `(A \ B) ⊔ (B \ A)`. -/
def symmDiff [Max α] [SDiff α] (a b : α) : α :=
  a \ b ⊔ b \ a

/-- The Heyting bi-implication is `(b ⇨ a) ⊓ (a ⇨ b)`. This generalizes equivalence of
propositions. -/
def bihimp [Min α] [HImp α] (a b : α) : α :=
  (b ⇨ a) ⊓ (a ⇨ b)

/-- Notation for symmDiff -/
scoped[symmDiff] infixl:100 " ∆ " => symmDiff

/-- Notation for bihimp -/
scoped[symmDiff] infixl:100 " ⇔ " => bihimp

open scoped symmDiff

theorem symmDiff_def [Max α] [SDiff α] (a b : α) : a ∆ b = a \ b ⊔ b \ a :=
  rfl

theorem bihimp_def [Min α] [HImp α] (a b : α) : a ⇔ b = (b ⇨ a) ⊓ (a ⇨ b) :=
  rfl

theorem symmDiff_eq_Xor' (p q : Prop) : p ∆ q = Xor' p q :=
  rfl

@[simp]
theorem bihimp_iff_iff {p q : Prop} : p ⇔ q ↔ (p ↔ q) :=
  iff_iff_implies_and_implies.symm.trans Iff.comm

@[simp]
theorem Bool.symmDiff_eq_xor : ∀ p q : Bool, p ∆ q = xor p q := by decide

  sup_le (sdiff_le_iff.2 ha) <| sdiff_le_iff.2 hb

theorem symmDiff_le_iff {a b c : α} : a ∆ b ≤ c ↔ a ≤ b ⊔ c ∧ b ≤ a ⊔ c := by
  simp_rw [symmDiff, sup_le_iff, sdiff_le_iff]

  sup_le_sup sdiff_le sdiff_le

theorem symmDiff_sdiff : a ∆ b \ c = a \ (b ⊔ c) ⊔ b \ (a ⊔ c) := by
  rw [symmDiff, sup_sdiff_distrib, sdiff_sdiff_left, sdiff_sdiff_left]

theorem symmDiff_sdiff_eq_sup : a ∆ (b \ a) = a ⊔ b := by
  rw [symmDiff, sdiff_idem]
  exact
    le_antisymm (sup_le_sup sdiff_le sdiff_le)
      (sup_le le_sdiff_sup <| le_sdiff_sup.trans <| sup_le le_sup_right le_sdiff_sup)

@[simp]
theorem sdiff_symmDiff_eq_sup : (a \ b) ∆ b = a ⊔ b := by
  rw [symmDiff_comm, symmDiff_sdiff_eq_sup, sup_comm]

@[simp]
theorem symmDiff_sup_inf : a ∆ b ⊔ a ⊓ b = a ⊔ b := by
  refine le_antisymm (sup_le symmDiff_le_sup inf_le_sup) ?_
  rw [sup_inf_left, symmDiff]
  refine sup_le (le_inf le_sup_right ?_) (le_inf ?_ le_sup_right)
  · rw [sup_right_comm]
    exact le_sup_of_le_left le_sdiff_sup
  · rw [sup_assoc]
    exact le_sup_of_le_right le_sdiff_sup

  rw [← symmDiff_sdiff_inf a, sdiff_symmDiff_eq_sup, symmDiff_sup_inf]

  rw [symmDiff_comm, symmDiff_symmDiff_inf]

theorem symmDiff_triangle : a ∆ c ≤ a ∆ b ⊔ b ∆ c := by
  refine (sup_le_sup (sdiff_triangle a b c) <| sdiff_triangle _ b _).trans_eq ?_
  rw [sup_comm (c \ b), sup_sup_sup_comm, symmDiff, symmDiff]

theorem le_symmDiff_sup_right (a b : α) : a ≤ (a ∆ b) ⊔ b := by
  convert symmDiff_triangle a b ⊥ <;> rw [symmDiff_bot]

theorem le_symmDiff_sup_left (a b : α) : b ≤ (a ∆ b) ⊔ a :=
  symmDiff_comm a b ▸ le_symmDiff_sup_right ..

theorem le_symmDiff_iff_right : b ≤ a ∆ b ↔ Disjoint a b := by
  rw [symmDiff_comm, le_symmDiff_iff_left, disjoint_comm]

theorem symmDiff_symmDiff_left :
    a ∆ b ∆ c = a \ (b ⊔ c) ⊔ b \ (a ⊔ c) ⊔ c \ (a ⊔ b) ⊔ a ⊓ b ⊓ c :=
  calc
    a ∆ b ∆ c = a ∆ b \ c ⊔ c \ a ∆ b := symmDiff_def _ _
    _ = a \ (b ⊔ c) ⊔ b \ (a ⊔ c) ⊔ (c \ (a ⊔ b) ⊔ c ⊓ a ⊓ b) := by
        { rw [sdiff_symmDiff', sup_comm (c ⊓ a ⊓ b), symmDiff_sdiff] }
    _ = a \ (b ⊔ c) ⊔ b \ (a ⊔ c) ⊔ c \ (a ⊔ b) ⊔ a ⊓ b ⊓ c := by ac_rfl

    a ∆ (b ∆ c) = a \ (b ⊔ c) ⊔ b \ (a ⊔ c) ⊔ c \ (a ⊔ b) ⊔ a ⊓ b ⊓ c :=
  calc
    a ∆ (b ∆ c) = a \ b ∆ c ⊔ b ∆ c \ a := symmDiff_def _ _
    _ = a \ (b ⊔ c) ⊔ a ⊓ b ⊓ c ⊔ (b \ (c ⊔ a) ⊔ c \ (b ⊔ a)) := by
        { rw [sdiff_symmDiff', sup_comm (a ⊓ b ⊓ c), symmDiff_sdiff] }
    _ = a \ (b ⊔ c) ⊔ b \ (a ⊔ c) ⊔ c \ (a ⊔ b) ⊔ a ⊓ b ⊓ c := by ac_rfl

import Mathlib.Order.BooleanAlgebra

import Mathlib.Logic.Equiv.Basic

/-!
# Symmetric difference and bi-implication

This file defines the symmetric difference and bi-implication operators in (co-)Heyting algebras.

## Examples

Some examples are
* The symmetric difference of two sets is the set of elements that are in either but not both.
* The symmetric difference on propositions is `Xor'`.
* The symmetric difference on `Bool` is `Bool.xor`.
* The equivalence of propositions. Two propositions are equivalent if they imply each other.
* The symmetric difference translates to addition when considering a Boolean algebra as a Boolean
  ring.

## Main declarations

* `symmDiff`: The symmetric difference operator, defined as `(a \ b) ⊔ (b \ a)`
* `bihimp`: The bi-implication operator, defined as `(b ⇨ a) ⊓ (a ⇨ b)`

In generalized Boolean algebras, the symmetric difference operator is:

* `symmDiff_comm`: commutative, and
* `symmDiff_assoc`: associative.

## Notations

* `a ∆ b`: `symmDiff a b`
* `a ⇔ b`: `bihimp a b`

## References

The proof of associativity follows the note "Associativity of the Symmetric Difference of Sets: A
Proof from the Book" by John McCuan:

* <https://people.math.gatech.edu/~mccuan/courses/4317/symmetricdifference.pdf>

## Tags

boolean ring, generalized boolean algebra, boolean algebra, symmetric difference, bi-implication,
Heyting
-/

assert_not_exists RelIso

open Function OrderDual

variable {ι α β : Type*} {π : ι → Type*}

/-- The symmetric difference operator on a type with `⊔` and `\` is `(A \ B) ⊔ (B \ A)`. -/
def symmDiff [Max α] [SDiff α] (a b : α) : α :=
  a \ b ⊔ b \ a

/-- The Heyting bi-implication is `(b ⇨ a) ⊓ (a ⇨ b)`. This generalizes equivalence of
propositions. -/
def bihimp [Min α] [HImp α] (a b : α) : α :=
  (b ⇨ a) ⊓ (a ⇨ b)

/-- Notation for symmDiff -/
scoped[symmDiff] infixl:100 " ∆ " => symmDiff

/-- Notation for bihimp -/
scoped[symmDiff] infixl:100 " ⇔ " => bihimp

open scoped symmDiff

theorem symmDiff_def [Max α] [SDiff α] (a b : α) : a ∆ b = a \ b ⊔ b \ a :=
  rfl

theorem bihimp_def [Min α] [HImp α] (a b : α) : a ⇔ b = (b ⇨ a) ⊓ (a ⇨ b) :=
  rfl

theorem symmDiff_eq_Xor' (p q : Prop) : p ∆ q = Xor' p q :=
  rfl

@[simp]
theorem bihimp_iff_iff {p q : Prop} : p ⇔ q ↔ (p ↔ q) :=
  iff_iff_implies_and_implies.symm.trans Iff.comm

@[simp]
theorem Bool.symmDiff_eq_xor : ∀ p q : Bool, p ∆ q = xor p q := by decide

section GeneralizedCoheytingAlgebra

instance symmDiff_isCommutative : Std.Commutative (α := α) (· ∆ ·) :=

@[simp]
theorem symmDiff_self : a ∆ a = ⊥ := by rw [symmDiff, sup_idem, sdiff_self]

@[simp]
theorem symmDiff_bot : a ∆ ⊥ = a := by rw [symmDiff, sdiff_bot, bot_sdiff, sup_bot_eq]

@[simp]

@[simp]
theorem symmDiff_eq_bot {a b : α} : a ∆ b = ⊥ ↔ a = b := by
  simp_rw [symmDiff, sup_eq_bot_iff, sdiff_eq_bot_iff, le_antisymm_iff]

theorem symmDiff_of_le {a b : α} (h : a ≤ b) : a ∆ b = b \ a := by
  rw [symmDiff, sdiff_eq_bot_iff.2 h, bot_sup_eq]

theorem symmDiff_of_ge {a b : α} (h : b ≤ a) : a ∆ b = a \ b := by
  rw [symmDiff, sdiff_eq_bot_iff.2 h, sup_bot_eq]

theorem symmDiff_le {a b c : α} (ha : a ≤ b ⊔ c) (hb : b ≤ a ⊔ c) : a ∆ b ≤ c :=
  sup_le (sdiff_le_iff.2 ha) <| sdiff_le_iff.2 hb

theorem symmDiff_le_iff {a b c : α} : a ∆ b ≤ c ↔ a ≤ b ⊔ c ∧ b ≤ a ⊔ c := by
  simp_rw [symmDiff, sup_le_iff, sdiff_le_iff]

@[simp]
theorem symmDiff_le_sup {a b : α} : a ∆ b ≤ a ⊔ b :=
  sup_le_sup sdiff_le sdiff_le

theorem symmDiff_eq_sup_sdiff_inf : a ∆ b = (a ⊔ b) \ (a ⊓ b) := by simp [sup_sdiff, symmDiff]

theorem Disjoint.symmDiff_eq_sup {a b : α} (h : Disjoint a b) : a ∆ b = a ⊔ b := by
  rw [symmDiff, h.sdiff_eq_left, h.sdiff_eq_right]

theorem symmDiff_sdiff : a ∆ b \ c = a \ (b ⊔ c) ⊔ b \ (a ⊔ c) := by
  rw [symmDiff, sup_sdiff_distrib, sdiff_sdiff_left, sdiff_sdiff_left]

@[simp]
theorem symmDiff_sdiff_inf : a ∆ b \ (a ⊓ b) = a ∆ b := by
  rw [symmDiff_sdiff]
  simp [symmDiff]

@[simp]
theorem symmDiff_sdiff_eq_sup : a ∆ (b \ a) = a ⊔ b := by
  rw [symmDiff, sdiff_idem]
  exact
    le_antisymm (sup_le_sup sdiff_le sdiff_le)
      (sup_le le_sdiff_sup <| le_sdiff_sup.trans <| sup_le le_sup_right le_sdiff_sup)

@[simp]
theorem sdiff_symmDiff_eq_sup : (a \ b) ∆ b = a ⊔ b := by
  rw [symmDiff_comm, symmDiff_sdiff_eq_sup, sup_comm]

@[simp]
theorem symmDiff_sup_inf : a ∆ b ⊔ a ⊓ b = a ⊔ b := by
  refine le_antisymm (sup_le symmDiff_le_sup inf_le_sup) ?_
  rw [sup_inf_left, symmDiff]
  refine sup_le (le_inf le_sup_right ?_) (le_inf ?_ le_sup_right)
  · rw [sup_right_comm]
    exact le_sup_of_le_left le_sdiff_sup
  · rw [sup_assoc]
    exact le_sup_of_le_right le_sdiff_sup

@[simp]
theorem inf_sup_symmDiff : a ⊓ b ⊔ a ∆ b = a ⊔ b := by rw [sup_comm, symmDiff_sup_inf]

@[simp]
theorem symmDiff_symmDiff_inf : a ∆ b ∆ (a ⊓ b) = a ⊔ b := by
  rw [← symmDiff_sdiff_inf a, sdiff_symmDiff_eq_sup, symmDiff_sup_inf]

@[simp]
theorem inf_symmDiff_symmDiff : (a ⊓ b) ∆ (a ∆ b) = a ⊔ b := by
  rw [symmDiff_comm, symmDiff_symmDiff_inf]

theorem symmDiff_triangle : a ∆ c ≤ a ∆ b ⊔ b ∆ c := by
  refine (sup_le_sup (sdiff_triangle a b c) <| sdiff_triangle _ b _).trans_eq ?_
  rw [sup_comm (c \ b), sup_sup_sup_comm, symmDiff, symmDiff]

theorem le_symmDiff_sup_right (a b : α) : a ≤ (a ∆ b) ⊔ b := by
  convert symmDiff_triangle a b ⊥ <;> rw [symmDiff_bot]

theorem le_symmDiff_sup_left (a b : α) : b ≤ (a ∆ b) ⊔ a :=
  symmDiff_comm a b ▸ le_symmDiff_sup_right ..

  rw [symmDiff_def, sup_sdiff, sdiff_idem, sdiff_sdiff_self, bot_sup_eq]

  refine ⟨fun h => ?_, Disjoint.symmDiff_eq_sup⟩
  rw [symmDiff_eq_sup_sdiff_inf, sdiff_eq_self_iff_disjoint] at h
  exact h.of_disjoint_inf_of_le le_sup_left

  refine ⟨fun h => ?_, fun h => h.symmDiff_eq_sup.symm ▸ le_sup_left⟩
  rw [symmDiff_eq_sup_sdiff_inf] at h
  exact disjoint_iff_inf_le.mpr (le_sdiff_right.1 <| inf_le_of_left_le h).le

@[simp]
theorem le_symmDiff_iff_right : b ≤ a ∆ b ↔ Disjoint a b := by
  rw [symmDiff_comm, le_symmDiff_iff_left, disjoint_comm]

theorem symmDiff_symmDiff_left :
    a ∆ b ∆ c = a \ (b ⊔ c) ⊔ b \ (a ⊔ c) ⊔ c \ (a ⊔ b) ⊔ a ⊓ b ⊓ c :=
  calc
    a ∆ b ∆ c = a ∆ b \ c ⊔ c \ a ∆ b := symmDiff_def _ _
    _ = a \ (b ⊔ c) ⊔ b \ (a ⊔ c) ⊔ (c \ (a ⊔ b) ⊔ c ⊓ a ⊓ b) := by
        { rw [sdiff_symmDiff', sup_comm (c ⊓ a ⊓ b), symmDiff_sdiff] }
    _ = a \ (b ⊔ c) ⊔ b \ (a ⊔ c) ⊔ c \ (a ⊔ b) ⊔ a ⊓ b ⊓ c := by ac_rfl

theorem symmDiff_symmDiff_right :
    a ∆ (b ∆ c) = a \ (b ⊔ c) ⊔ b \ (a ⊔ c) ⊔ c \ (a ⊔ b) ⊔ a ⊓ b ⊓ c :=
  calc
    a ∆ (b ∆ c) = a \ b ∆ c ⊔ b ∆ c \ a := symmDiff_def _ _
    _ = a \ (b ⊔ c) ⊔ a ⊓ b ⊓ c ⊔ (b \ (c ⊔ a) ⊔ c \ (b ⊔ a)) := by
        { rw [sdiff_symmDiff', sup_comm (a ⊓ b ⊓ c), symmDiff_sdiff] }
    _ = a \ (b ⊔ c) ⊔ b \ (a ⊔ c) ⊔ c \ (a ⊔ b) ⊔ a ⊓ b ⊓ c := by ac_rfl

  rw [symmDiff_symmDiff_left, symmDiff_symmDiff_right]

import Mathlib.Order.BooleanAlgebra

import Mathlib.Logic.Equiv.Basic

/-!
# Symmetric difference and bi-implication

This file defines the symmetric difference and bi-implication operators in (co-)Heyting algebras.

## Examples

Some examples are
* The symmetric difference of two sets is the set of elements that are in either but not both.
* The symmetric difference on propositions is `Xor'`.
* The symmetric difference on `Bool` is `Bool.xor`.
* The equivalence of propositions. Two propositions are equivalent if they imply each other.
* The symmetric difference translates to addition when considering a Boolean algebra as a Boolean
  ring.

## Main declarations

* `symmDiff`: The symmetric difference operator, defined as `(a \ b) ⊔ (b \ a)`
* `bihimp`: The bi-implication operator, defined as `(b ⇨ a) ⊓ (a ⇨ b)`

In generalized Boolean algebras, the symmetric difference operator is:

* `symmDiff_comm`: commutative, and
* `symmDiff_assoc`: associative.

## Notations

* `a ∆ b`: `symmDiff a b`
* `a ⇔ b`: `bihimp a b`

## References

The proof of associativity follows the note "Associativity of the Symmetric Difference of Sets: A
Proof from the Book" by John McCuan:

* <https://people.math.gatech.edu/~mccuan/courses/4317/symmetricdifference.pdf>

## Tags

boolean ring, generalized boolean algebra, boolean algebra, symmetric difference, bi-implication,
Heyting
-/

open Function OrderDual

variable {ι α β : Type*} {π : ι → Type*}

/-- The symmetric difference operator on a type with `⊔` and `\` is `(A \ B) ⊔ (B \ A)`. -/
def symmDiff [Max α] [SDiff α] (a b : α) : α :=
  a \ b ⊔ b \ a

/-- The Heyting bi-implication is `(b ⇨ a) ⊓ (a ⇨ b)`. This generalizes equivalence of
propositions. -/
def bihimp [Min α] [HImp α] (a b : α) : α :=
  (b ⇨ a) ⊓ (a ⇨ b)

/-- Notation for symmDiff -/
scoped[symmDiff] infixl:100 " ∆ " => symmDiff

/-- Notation for bihimp -/
scoped[symmDiff] infixl:100 " ⇔ " => bihimp

open scoped symmDiff

theorem symmDiff_def [Max α] [SDiff α] (a b : α) : a ∆ b = a \ b ⊔ b \ a :=
  rfl

theorem bihimp_def [Min α] [HImp α] (a b : α) : a ⇔ b = (b ⇨ a) ⊓ (a ⇨ b) :=
  rfl

theorem symmDiff_eq_Xor' (p q : Prop) : p ∆ q = Xor' p q :=
  rfl

@[simp]
theorem bihimp_iff_iff {p q : Prop} : p ⇔ q ↔ (p ↔ q) :=
  iff_iff_implies_and_implies.symm.trans Iff.comm

@[simp]
theorem Bool.symmDiff_eq_xor : ∀ p q : Bool, p ∆ q = xor p q := by decide

section GeneralizedCoheytingAlgebra

@[simp]

  rfl

theorem symmDiff_comm : a ∆ b = b ∆ a := by simp only [symmDiff, sup_comm]

instance symmDiff_isCommutative : Std.Commutative (α := α) (· ∆ ·) :=
  ⟨symmDiff_comm⟩

@[simp]
theorem symmDiff_self : a ∆ a = ⊥ := by rw [symmDiff, sup_idem, sdiff_self]

@[simp]
theorem symmDiff_bot : a ∆ ⊥ = a := by rw [symmDiff, sdiff_bot, bot_sdiff, sup_bot_eq]

@[simp]
theorem bot_symmDiff : ⊥ ∆ a = a := by rw [symmDiff_comm, symmDiff_bot]

@[simp]
theorem symmDiff_eq_bot {a b : α} : a ∆ b = ⊥ ↔ a = b := by
  simp_rw [symmDiff, sup_eq_bot_iff, sdiff_eq_bot_iff, le_antisymm_iff]

theorem symmDiff_of_le {a b : α} (h : a ≤ b) : a ∆ b = b \ a := by
  rw [symmDiff, sdiff_eq_bot_iff.2 h, bot_sup_eq]

theorem symmDiff_of_ge {a b : α} (h : b ≤ a) : a ∆ b = a \ b := by
  rw [symmDiff, sdiff_eq_bot_iff.2 h, sup_bot_eq]

theorem symmDiff_le {a b c : α} (ha : a ≤ b ⊔ c) (hb : b ≤ a ⊔ c) : a ∆ b ≤ c :=
  sup_le (sdiff_le_iff.2 ha) <| sdiff_le_iff.2 hb

theorem symmDiff_le_iff {a b c : α} : a ∆ b ≤ c ↔ a ≤ b ⊔ c ∧ b ≤ a ⊔ c := by
  simp_rw [symmDiff, sup_le_iff, sdiff_le_iff]

@[simp]
theorem symmDiff_le_sup {a b : α} : a ∆ b ≤ a ⊔ b :=
  sup_le_sup sdiff_le sdiff_le

theorem symmDiff_eq_sup_sdiff_inf : a ∆ b = (a ⊔ b) \ (a ⊓ b) := by simp [sup_sdiff, symmDiff]

theorem Disjoint.symmDiff_eq_sup {a b : α} (h : Disjoint a b) : a ∆ b = a ⊔ b := by
  rw [symmDiff, h.sdiff_eq_left, h.sdiff_eq_right]

theorem symmDiff_sdiff : a ∆ b \ c = a \ (b ⊔ c) ⊔ b \ (a ⊔ c) := by
  rw [symmDiff, sup_sdiff_distrib, sdiff_sdiff_left, sdiff_sdiff_left]

@[simp]
theorem symmDiff_sdiff_inf : a ∆ b \ (a ⊓ b) = a ∆ b := by
  rw [symmDiff_sdiff]
  simp [symmDiff]

@[simp]
theorem symmDiff_sdiff_eq_sup : a ∆ (b \ a) = a ⊔ b := by
  rw [symmDiff, sdiff_idem]
  exact
    le_antisymm (sup_le_sup sdiff_le sdiff_le)
      (sup_le le_sdiff_sup <| le_sdiff_sup.trans <| sup_le le_sup_right le_sdiff_sup)

@[simp]
theorem sdiff_symmDiff_eq_sup : (a \ b) ∆ b = a ⊔ b := by
  rw [symmDiff_comm, symmDiff_sdiff_eq_sup, sup_comm]

@[simp]
theorem symmDiff_sup_inf : a ∆ b ⊔ a ⊓ b = a ⊔ b := by
  refine le_antisymm (sup_le symmDiff_le_sup inf_le_sup) ?_
  rw [sup_inf_left, symmDiff]
  refine sup_le (le_inf le_sup_right ?_) (le_inf ?_ le_sup_right)
  · rw [sup_right_comm]
    exact le_sup_of_le_left le_sdiff_sup
  · rw [sup_assoc]
    exact le_sup_of_le_right le_sdiff_sup

@[simp]
theorem inf_sup_symmDiff : a ⊓ b ⊔ a ∆ b = a ⊔ b := by rw [sup_comm, symmDiff_sup_inf]

@[simp]
theorem symmDiff_symmDiff_inf : a ∆ b ∆ (a ⊓ b) = a ⊔ b := by
  rw [← symmDiff_sdiff_inf a, sdiff_symmDiff_eq_sup, symmDiff_sup_inf]

@[simp]
theorem inf_symmDiff_symmDiff : (a ⊓ b) ∆ (a ∆ b) = a ⊔ b := by
  rw [symmDiff_comm, symmDiff_symmDiff_inf]

theorem symmDiff_triangle : a ∆ c ≤ a ∆ b ⊔ b ∆ c := by
  refine (sup_le_sup (sdiff_triangle a b c) <| sdiff_triangle _ b _).trans_eq ?_
  rw [sup_comm (c \ b), sup_sup_sup_comm, symmDiff, symmDiff]

theorem le_symmDiff_sup_right (a b : α) : a ≤ (a ∆ b) ⊔ b := by
  convert symmDiff_triangle a b ⊥ <;> rw [symmDiff_bot]

theorem le_symmDiff_sup_left (a b : α) : b ≤ (a ∆ b) ⊔ a :=
  symmDiff_comm a b ▸ le_symmDiff_sup_right ..

  rw [sdiff_symmDiff, sdiff_sup]

  exact h.of_disjoint_inf_of_le le_sup_left

  refine ⟨fun h => ?_, fun h => h.symmDiff_eq_sup.symm ▸ le_sup_left⟩
  rw [symmDiff_eq_sup_sdiff_inf] at h
  exact disjoint_iff_inf_le.mpr (le_sdiff_right.1 <| inf_le_of_left_le h).le

@[simp]
theorem le_symmDiff_iff_right : b ≤ a ∆ b ↔ Disjoint a b := by
  rw [symmDiff_comm, le_symmDiff_iff_left, disjoint_comm]

theorem symmDiff_symmDiff_left :
    a ∆ b ∆ c = a \ (b ⊔ c) ⊔ b \ (a ⊔ c) ⊔ c \ (a ⊔ b) ⊔ a ⊓ b ⊓ c :=
  calc
    a ∆ b ∆ c = a ∆ b \ c ⊔ c \ a ∆ b := symmDiff_def _ _
    _ = a \ (b ⊔ c) ⊔ b \ (a ⊔ c) ⊔ (c \ (a ⊔ b) ⊔ c ⊓ a ⊓ b) := by
        { rw [sdiff_symmDiff', sup_comm (c ⊓ a ⊓ b), symmDiff_sdiff] }
    _ = a \ (b ⊔ c) ⊔ b \ (a ⊔ c) ⊔ c \ (a ⊔ b) ⊔ a ⊓ b ⊓ c := by ac_rfl

theorem symmDiff_symmDiff_right :
    a ∆ (b ∆ c) = a \ (b ⊔ c) ⊔ b \ (a ⊔ c) ⊔ c \ (a ⊔ b) ⊔ a ⊓ b ⊓ c :=
  calc
    a ∆ (b ∆ c) = a \ b ∆ c ⊔ b ∆ c \ a := symmDiff_def _ _
    _ = a \ (b ⊔ c) ⊔ a ⊓ b ⊓ c ⊔ (b \ (c ⊔ a) ⊔ c \ (b ⊔ a)) := by
        { rw [sdiff_symmDiff', sup_comm (a ⊓ b ⊓ c), symmDiff_sdiff] }
    _ = a \ (b ⊔ c) ⊔ b \ (a ⊔ c) ⊔ c \ (a ⊔ b) ⊔ a ⊓ b ⊓ c := by ac_rfl

  rw [symmDiff_symmDiff_left, symmDiff_symmDiff_right]

  simp_rw [← symmDiff_assoc, symmDiff_comm]

theorem symmDiff_right_comm : a ∆ b ∆ c = a ∆ c ∆ b := by simp_rw [symmDiff_assoc, symmDiff_comm]

theorem symmDiff_symmDiff_symmDiff_comm : a ∆ b ∆ (c ∆ d) = a ∆ c ∆ (b ∆ d) := by
  simp_rw [symmDiff_assoc, symmDiff_left_comm]

@[simp]
theorem symmDiff_symmDiff_cancel_right : b ∆ a ∆ a = b := by simp [symmDiff_assoc]

@[simp]

  rw [symmDiff_comm, symmDiff_symmDiff_cancel_left]

theorem symmDiff_left_involutive (a : α) : Involutive (· ∆ a) :=
  symmDiff_symmDiff_cancel_right _

theorem symmDiff_right_involutive (a : α) : Involutive (a ∆ ·) :=
  symmDiff_symmDiff_cancel_left _

import Mathlib.Order.BooleanAlgebra

import Mathlib.Logic.Equiv.Basic

/-!
# Symmetric difference and bi-implication

This file defines the symmetric difference and bi-implication operators in (co-)Heyting algebras.

## Examples

Some examples are
* The symmetric difference of two sets is the set of elements that are in either but not both.
* The symmetric difference on propositions is `Xor'`.
* The symmetric difference on `Bool` is `Bool.xor`.
* The equivalence of propositions. Two propositions are equivalent if they imply each other.
* The symmetric difference translates to addition when considering a Boolean algebra as a Boolean
  ring.

## Main declarations

* `symmDiff`: The symmetric difference operator, defined as `(a \ b) ⊔ (b \ a)`
* `bihimp`: The bi-implication operator, defined as `(b ⇨ a) ⊓ (a ⇨ b)`

In generalized Boolean algebras, the symmetric difference operator is:

* `symmDiff_comm`: commutative, and
* `symmDiff_assoc`: associative.

## Notations

* `a ∆ b`: `symmDiff a b`
* `a ⇔ b`: `bihimp a b`

## References

The proof of associativity follows the note "Associativity of the Symmetric Difference of Sets: A
Proof from the Book" by John McCuan:

* <https://people.math.gatech.edu/~mccuan/courses/4317/symmetricdifference.pdf>

## Tags

boolean ring, generalized boolean algebra, boolean algebra, symmetric difference, bi-implication,
Heyting
-/

variable {ι α β : Type*} {π : ι → Type*}

/-- The symmetric difference operator on a type with `⊔` and `\` is `(A \ B) ⊔ (B \ A)`. -/
def symmDiff [Max α] [SDiff α] (a b : α) : α :=
  a \ b ⊔ b \ a

/-- The Heyting bi-implication is `(b ⇨ a) ⊓ (a ⇨ b)`. This generalizes equivalence of
propositions. -/
def bihimp [Min α] [HImp α] (a b : α) : α :=
  (b ⇨ a) ⊓ (a ⇨ b)

/-- Notation for symmDiff -/
scoped[symmDiff] infixl:100 " ∆ " => symmDiff

/-- Notation for bihimp -/
scoped[symmDiff] infixl:100 " ⇔ " => bihimp

theorem symmDiff_def [Max α] [SDiff α] (a b : α) : a ∆ b = a \ b ⊔ b \ a :=
  rfl

theorem bihimp_def [Min α] [HImp α] (a b : α) : a ⇔ b = (b ⇨ a) ⊓ (a ⇨ b) :=
  rfl

theorem symmDiff_eq_Xor' (p q : Prop) : p ∆ q = Xor' p q :=

  rw [symmDiff_comm, symmDiff_sdiff_eq_sup, sup_comm]

  rw [sup_inf_left, symmDiff]
  refine sup_le (le_inf le_sup_right ?_) (le_inf ?_ le_sup_right)
  · rw [sup_right_comm]
    exact le_sup_of_le_left le_sdiff_sup
  · rw [sup_assoc]
    exact le_sup_of_le_right le_sdiff_sup

  rw [symmDiff_comm, symmDiff_symmDiff_inf]

  refine (sup_le_sup (sdiff_triangle a b c) <| sdiff_triangle _ b _).trans_eq ?_
  rw [sup_comm (c \ b), sup_sup_sup_comm, symmDiff, symmDiff]

theorem le_symmDiff_sup_right (a b : α) : a ≤ (a ∆ b) ⊔ b := by
  convert symmDiff_triangle a b ⊥ <;> rw [symmDiff_bot]

theorem le_symmDiff_sup_left (a b : α) : b ≤ (a ∆ b) ⊔ a :=
  symmDiff_comm a b ▸ le_symmDiff_sup_right ..

This file defines the symmetric difference and bi-implication operators in (co-)Heyting algebras.

# Symmetric difference and bi-implication

This file defines the symmetric difference and bi-implication operators in (co-)Heyting algebras.

## Examples

Some examples are
* The symmetric difference of two sets is the set of elements that are in either but not both.
* The symmetric difference on propositions is `Xor'`.
* The symmetric difference on `Bool` is `Bool.xor`.
* The equivalence of propositions. Two propositions are equivalent if they imply each other.
* The symmetric difference translates to addition when considering a Boolean algebra as a Boolean
  ring.

## Main declarations

* `symmDiff`: The symmetric difference operator, defined as `(a \ b) ⊔ (b \ a)`
* `bihimp`: The bi-implication operator, defined as `(b ⇨ a) ⊓ (a ⇨ b)`

In generalized Boolean algebras, the symmetric difference operator is:

* `symmDiff_comm`: commutative, and
* `symmDiff_assoc`: associative.

## Notations

* `a ∆ b`: `symmDiff a b`
* `a ⇔ b`: `bihimp a b`

## References

The proof of associativity follows the note "Associativity of the Symmetric Difference of Sets: A
Proof from the Book" by John McCuan:

* <https://people.math.gatech.edu/~mccuan/courses/4317/symmetricdifference.pdf>

Heyting

/-!
# Symmetric difference and bi-implication

This file defines the symmetric difference and bi-implication operators in (co-)Heyting algebras.

## Examples

Some examples are
* The symmetric difference of two sets is the set of elements that are in either but not both.
* The symmetric difference on propositions is `Xor'`.
* The symmetric difference on `Bool` is `Bool.xor`.
* The equivalence of propositions. Two propositions are equivalent if they imply each other.
* The symmetric difference translates to addition when considering a Boolean algebra as a Boolean
  ring.

## Main declarations

* `symmDiff`: The symmetric difference operator, defined as `(a \ b) ⊔ (b \ a)`
* `bihimp`: The bi-implication operator, defined as `(b ⇨ a) ⊓ (a ⇨ b)`

In generalized Boolean algebras, the symmetric difference operator is:

* `symmDiff_comm`: commutative, and
* `symmDiff_assoc`: associative.

## Notations

* `a ∆ b`: `symmDiff a b`
* `a ⇔ b`: `bihimp a b`

## References

The proof of associativity follows the note "Associativity of the Symmetric Difference of Sets: A
Proof from the Book" by John McCuan:

* <https://people.math.gatech.edu/~mccuan/courses/4317/symmetricdifference.pdf>

## Tags

boolean ring, generalized boolean algebra, boolean algebra, symmetric difference, bi-implication,
Heyting
-/

/-- The symmetric difference operator on a type with `⊔` and `\` is `(A \ B) ⊔ (B \ A)`. -/
def symmDiff [Max α] [SDiff α] (a b : α) : α :=
  a \ b ⊔ b \ a

/-- The Heyting bi-implication is `(b ⇨ a) ⊓ (a ⇨ b)`. This generalizes equivalence of
propositions. -/
def bihimp [Min α] [HImp α] (a b : α) : α :=
  (b ⇨ a) ⊓ (a ⇨ b)

/-- Notation for symmDiff -/

/-- Notation for bihimp -/
scoped[symmDiff] infixl:100 " ⇔ " => bihimp

/-!
# Symmetric difference and bi-implication

This file defines the symmetric difference and bi-implication operators in (co-)Heyting algebras.

## Examples

Some examples are
* The symmetric difference of two sets is the set of elements that are in either but not both.
* The symmetric difference on propositions is `Xor'`.
* The symmetric difference on `Bool` is `Bool.xor`.
* The equivalence of propositions. Two propositions are equivalent if they imply each other.
* The symmetric difference translates to addition when considering a Boolean algebra as a Boolean
  ring.

## Main declarations

* `symmDiff`: The symmetric difference operator, defined as `(a \ b) ⊔ (b \ a)`
* `bihimp`: The bi-implication operator, defined as `(b ⇨ a) ⊓ (a ⇨ b)`

In generalized Boolean algebras, the symmetric difference operator is:

* `symmDiff_comm`: commutative, and
* `symmDiff_assoc`: associative.

## Notations

* `a ∆ b`: `symmDiff a b`
* `a ⇔ b`: `bihimp a b`

## References

The proof of associativity follows the note "Associativity of the Symmetric Difference of Sets: A
Proof from the Book" by John McCuan:

* <https://people.math.gatech.edu/~mccuan/courses/4317/symmetricdifference.pdf>

## Tags

boolean ring, generalized boolean algebra, boolean algebra, symmetric difference, bi-implication,
Heyting
-/

open Function OrderDual

variable {ι α β : Type*} {π : ι → Type*}

/-- The symmetric difference operator on a type with `⊔` and `\` is `(A \ B) ⊔ (B \ A)`. -/
def symmDiff [Max α] [SDiff α] (a b : α) : α :=
  a \ b ⊔ b \ a

/-- The Heyting bi-implication is `(b ⇨ a) ⊓ (a ⇨ b)`. This generalizes equivalence of
propositions. -/
def bihimp [Min α] [HImp α] (a b : α) : α :=
  (b ⇨ a) ⊓ (a ⇨ b)

/-- Notation for symmDiff -/
scoped[symmDiff] infixl:100 " ∆ " => symmDiff

/-- Notation for bihimp -/
scoped[symmDiff] infixl:100 " ⇔ " => bihimp

  rfl

theorem bihimp_def [Min α] [HImp α] (a b : α) : a ⇔ b = (b ⇨ a) ⊓ (a ⇨ b) :=
  rfl

  rfl

/-!
# Symmetric difference and bi-implication

This file defines the symmetric difference and bi-implication operators in (co-)Heyting algebras.

## Examples

Some examples are
* The symmetric difference of two sets is the set of elements that are in either but not both.
* The symmetric difference on propositions is `Xor'`.
* The symmetric difference on `Bool` is `Bool.xor`.
* The equivalence of propositions. Two propositions are equivalent if they imply each other.
* The symmetric difference translates to addition when considering a Boolean algebra as a Boolean
  ring.

## Main declarations

* `symmDiff`: The symmetric difference operator, defined as `(a \ b) ⊔ (b \ a)`
* `bihimp`: The bi-implication operator, defined as `(b ⇨ a) ⊓ (a ⇨ b)`

In generalized Boolean algebras, the symmetric difference operator is:

* `symmDiff_comm`: commutative, and
* `symmDiff_assoc`: associative.

## Notations

* `a ∆ b`: `symmDiff a b`
* `a ⇔ b`: `bihimp a b`

## References

The proof of associativity follows the note "Associativity of the Symmetric Difference of Sets: A
Proof from the Book" by John McCuan:

* <https://people.math.gatech.edu/~mccuan/courses/4317/symmetricdifference.pdf>

## Tags

boolean ring, generalized boolean algebra, boolean algebra, symmetric difference, bi-implication,
Heyting
-/

variable {ι α β : Type*} {π : ι → Type*}

/-- The symmetric difference operator on a type with `⊔` and `\` is `(A \ B) ⊔ (B \ A)`. -/
def symmDiff [Max α] [SDiff α] (a b : α) : α :=
  a \ b ⊔ b \ a

/-- The Heyting bi-implication is `(b ⇨ a) ⊓ (a ⇨ b)`. This generalizes equivalence of
propositions. -/
def bihimp [Min α] [HImp α] (a b : α) : α :=
  (b ⇨ a) ⊓ (a ⇨ b)

/-- Notation for symmDiff -/
scoped[symmDiff] infixl:100 " ∆ " => symmDiff

/-- Notation for bihimp -/
scoped[symmDiff] infixl:100 " ⇔ " => bihimp

theorem symmDiff_def [Max α] [SDiff α] (a b : α) : a ∆ b = a \ b ⊔ b \ a :=
  rfl

theorem bihimp_def [Min α] [HImp α] (a b : α) : a ⇔ b = (b ⇨ a) ⊓ (a ⇨ b) :=
  rfl

  rfl

/-!
# Symmetric difference and bi-implication

This file defines the symmetric difference and bi-implication operators in (co-)Heyting algebras.

## Examples

Some examples are
* The symmetric difference of two sets is the set of elements that are in either but not both.
* The symmetric difference on propositions is `Xor'`.
* The symmetric difference on `Bool` is `Bool.xor`.
* The equivalence of propositions. Two propositions are equivalent if they imply each other.
* The symmetric difference translates to addition when considering a Boolean algebra as a Boolean
  ring.

## Main declarations

* `symmDiff`: The symmetric difference operator, defined as `(a \ b) ⊔ (b \ a)`
* `bihimp`: The bi-implication operator, defined as `(b ⇨ a) ⊓ (a ⇨ b)`

In generalized Boolean algebras, the symmetric difference operator is:

* `symmDiff_comm`: commutative, and
* `symmDiff_assoc`: associative.

## Notations

* `a ∆ b`: `symmDiff a b`
* `a ⇔ b`: `bihimp a b`

## References

The proof of associativity follows the note "Associativity of the Symmetric Difference of Sets: A
Proof from the Book" by John McCuan:

* <https://people.math.gatech.edu/~mccuan/courses/4317/symmetricdifference.pdf>

## Tags

Heyting
-/

/-- The symmetric difference operator on a type with `⊔` and `\` is `(A \ B) ⊔ (B \ A)`. -/
def symmDiff [Max α] [SDiff α] (a b : α) : α :=
  a \ b ⊔ b \ a

/-- The Heyting bi-implication is `(b ⇨ a) ⊓ (a ⇨ b)`. This generalizes equivalence of
propositions. -/
def bihimp [Min α] [HImp α] (a b : α) : α :=
  (b ⇨ a) ⊓ (a ⇨ b)

/-- Notation for symmDiff -/
scoped[symmDiff] infixl:100 " ∆ " => symmDiff

/-- Notation for bihimp -/
scoped[symmDiff] infixl:100 " ⇔ " => bihimp

theorem symmDiff_def [Max α] [SDiff α] (a b : α) : a ∆ b = a \ b ⊔ b \ a :=
  rfl

theorem bihimp_def [Min α] [HImp α] (a b : α) : a ⇔ b = (b ⇨ a) ⊓ (a ⇨ b) :=
  rfl

    a ∆ (b ∆ c) = a \ b ∆ c ⊔ b ∆ c \ a := symmDiff_def _ _

    _ = a \ (b ⊔ c) ⊔ b \ (a ⊔ c) ⊔ c \ (a ⊔ b) ⊔ a ⊓ b ⊓ c := by ac_rfl

  rw [symmDiff_symmDiff_left, symmDiff_symmDiff_right]

import Mathlib.Order.BooleanAlgebra

/-!
# Symmetric difference and bi-implication

This file defines the symmetric difference and bi-implication operators in (co-)Heyting algebras.

## Examples

Some examples are
* The symmetric difference of two sets is the set of elements that are in either but not both.
* The symmetric difference on propositions is `Xor'`.
* The symmetric difference on `Bool` is `Bool.xor`.
* The equivalence of propositions. Two propositions are equivalent if they imply each other.
* The symmetric difference translates to addition when considering a Boolean algebra as a Boolean
  ring.

## Main declarations

* `symmDiff`: The symmetric difference operator, defined as `(a \ b) ⊔ (b \ a)`
* `bihimp`: The bi-implication operator, defined as `(b ⇨ a) ⊓ (a ⇨ b)`

In generalized Boolean algebras, the symmetric difference operator is:

* `symmDiff_comm`: commutative, and
* `symmDiff_assoc`: associative.

## Notations

* `a ∆ b`: `symmDiff a b`
* `a ⇔ b`: `bihimp a b`

## References

The proof of associativity follows the note "Associativity of the Symmetric Difference of Sets: A
Proof from the Book" by John McCuan:

* <https://people.math.gatech.edu/~mccuan/courses/4317/symmetricdifference.pdf>

## Tags

boolean ring, generalized boolean algebra, boolean algebra, symmetric difference, bi-implication,
Heyting
-/

import Mathlib.Order.BooleanAlgebra

/-!
# Symmetric difference and bi-implication

This file defines the symmetric difference and bi-implication operators in (co-)Heyting algebras.

## Examples

Some examples are
* The symmetric difference of two sets is the set of elements that are in either but not both.
* The symmetric difference on propositions is `Xor'`.
* The symmetric difference on `Bool` is `Bool.xor`.
* The equivalence of propositions. Two propositions are equivalent if they imply each other.
* The symmetric difference translates to addition when considering a Boolean algebra as a Boolean
  ring.

## Main declarations

* `symmDiff`: The symmetric difference operator, defined as `(a \ b) ⊔ (b \ a)`
* `bihimp`: The bi-implication operator, defined as `(b ⇨ a) ⊓ (a ⇨ b)`

In generalized Boolean algebras, the symmetric difference operator is:

* `symmDiff_comm`: commutative, and
* `symmDiff_assoc`: associative.

## Notations

* `a ∆ b`: `symmDiff a b`
* `a ⇔ b`: `bihimp a b`

## References

The proof of associativity follows the note "Associativity of the Symmetric Difference of Sets: A
Proof from the Book" by John McCuan:

* <https://people.math.gatech.edu/~mccuan/courses/4317/symmetricdifference.pdf>

## Tags

boolean ring, generalized boolean algebra, boolean algebra, symmetric difference, bi-implication,
Heyting
-/

open Function OrderDual

variable {ι α β : Type*} {π : ι → Type*}

/-- The symmetric difference operator on a type with `⊔` and `\` is `(A \ B) ⊔ (B \ A)`. -/
def symmDiff [Max α] [SDiff α] (a b : α) : α :=
  a \ b ⊔ b \ a

/-- The Heyting bi-implication is `(b ⇨ a) ⊓ (a ⇨ b)`. This generalizes equivalence of
propositions. -/
def bihimp [Min α] [HImp α] (a b : α) : α :=
  (b ⇨ a) ⊓ (a ⇨ b)

/-- Notation for symmDiff -/
scoped[symmDiff] infixl:100 " ∆ " => symmDiff

/-- Notation for bihimp -/
scoped[symmDiff] infixl:100 " ⇔ " => bihimp

theorem symmDiff_def [Max α] [SDiff α] (a b : α) : a ∆ b = a \ b ⊔ b \ a :=
  rfl

theorem bihimp_def [Min α] [HImp α] (a b : α) : a ⇔ b = (b ⇨ a) ⊓ (a ⇨ b) :=
  rfl

  rfl

  iff_iff_implies_and_implies.symm.trans Iff.comm

/-!
# Symmetric difference and bi-implication

This file defines the symmetric difference and bi-implication operators in (co-)Heyting algebras.

## Examples

Some examples are
* The symmetric difference of two sets is the set of elements that are in either but not both.
* The symmetric difference on propositions is `Xor'`.
* The symmetric difference on `Bool` is `Bool.xor`.
* The equivalence of propositions. Two propositions are equivalent if they imply each other.
* The symmetric difference translates to addition when considering a Boolean algebra as a Boolean
  ring.

## Main declarations

* `symmDiff`: The symmetric difference operator, defined as `(a \ b) ⊔ (b \ a)`
* `bihimp`: The bi-implication operator, defined as `(b ⇨ a) ⊓ (a ⇨ b)`

In generalized Boolean algebras, the symmetric difference operator is:

* `symmDiff_comm`: commutative, and
* `symmDiff_assoc`: associative.

## Notations

* `a ∆ b`: `symmDiff a b`
* `a ⇔ b`: `bihimp a b`

## References

The proof of associativity follows the note "Associativity of the Symmetric Difference of Sets: A
Proof from the Book" by John McCuan:

* <https://people.math.gatech.edu/~mccuan/courses/4317/symmetricdifference.pdf>

## Tags

boolean ring, generalized boolean algebra, boolean algebra, symmetric difference, bi-implication,
Heyting
-/

open Function OrderDual

variable {ι α β : Type*} {π : ι → Type*}

/-- The symmetric difference operator on a type with `⊔` and `\` is `(A \ B) ⊔ (B \ A)`. -/
def symmDiff [Max α] [SDiff α] (a b : α) : α :=
  a \ b ⊔ b \ a

/-- The Heyting bi-implication is `(b ⇨ a) ⊓ (a ⇨ b)`. This generalizes equivalence of
propositions. -/
def bihimp [Min α] [HImp α] (a b : α) : α :=
  (b ⇨ a) ⊓ (a ⇨ b)

/-- Notation for symmDiff -/
scoped[symmDiff] infixl:100 " ∆ " => symmDiff

/-- Notation for bihimp -/
scoped[symmDiff] infixl:100 " ⇔ " => bihimp

open scoped symmDiff

theorem symmDiff_def [Max α] [SDiff α] (a b : α) : a ∆ b = a \ b ⊔ b \ a :=
  rfl

theorem bihimp_def [Min α] [HImp α] (a b : α) : a ⇔ b = (b ⇨ a) ⊓ (a ⇨ b) :=
  rfl

theorem symmDiff_eq_Xor' (p q : Prop) : p ∆ q = Xor' p q :=
  rfl

theorem bihimp_iff_iff {p q : Prop} : p ⇔ q ↔ (p ↔ q) :=
  iff_iff_implies_and_implies.symm.trans Iff.comm

@[simp]
theorem Bool.symmDiff_eq_xor : ∀ p q : Bool, p ∆ q = xor p q := by decide

  refine sup_le (le_inf le_sup_right ?_) (le_inf ?_ le_sup_right)
  · rw [sup_right_comm]

  · rw [sup_assoc]
    exact le_sup_of_le_right le_sdiff_sup

  symmDiff_comm a b ▸ le_symmDiff_sup_right ..

/-!
# Symmetric difference and bi-implication

This file defines the symmetric difference and bi-implication operators in (co-)Heyting algebras.

## Examples

Some examples are
* The symmetric difference of two sets is the set of elements that are in either but not both.
* The symmetric difference on propositions is `Xor'`.
* The symmetric difference on `Bool` is `Bool.xor`.
* The equivalence of propositions. Two propositions are equivalent if they imply each other.
* The symmetric difference translates to addition when considering a Boolean algebra as a Boolean
  ring.

## Main declarations

* `symmDiff`: The symmetric difference operator, defined as `(a \ b) ⊔ (b \ a)`
* `bihimp`: The bi-implication operator, defined as `(b ⇨ a) ⊓ (a ⇨ b)`

In generalized Boolean algebras, the symmetric difference operator is:

* `symmDiff_comm`: commutative, and
* `symmDiff_assoc`: associative.

## Notations

* `a ∆ b`: `symmDiff a b`
* `a ⇔ b`: `bihimp a b`

## References

The proof of associativity follows the note "Associativity of the Symmetric Difference of Sets: A
Proof from the Book" by John McCuan:

* <https://people.math.gatech.edu/~mccuan/courses/4317/symmetricdifference.pdf>

## Tags

boolean ring, generalized boolean algebra, boolean algebra, symmetric difference, bi-implication,
Heyting
-/

import Mathlib.Order.BooleanAlgebra

/-!
# Symmetric difference and bi-implication

This file defines the symmetric difference and bi-implication operators in (co-)Heyting algebras.

## Examples

Some examples are
* The symmetric difference of two sets is the set of elements that are in either but not both.
* The symmetric difference on propositions is `Xor'`.
* The symmetric difference on `Bool` is `Bool.xor`.
* The equivalence of propositions. Two propositions are equivalent if they imply each other.
* The symmetric difference translates to addition when considering a Boolean algebra as a Boolean
  ring.

## Main declarations

* `symmDiff`: The symmetric difference operator, defined as `(a \ b) ⊔ (b \ a)`
* `bihimp`: The bi-implication operator, defined as `(b ⇨ a) ⊓ (a ⇨ b)`

In generalized Boolean algebras, the symmetric difference operator is:

* `symmDiff_comm`: commutative, and
* `symmDiff_assoc`: associative.

## Notations

* `a ∆ b`: `symmDiff a b`
* `a ⇔ b`: `bihimp a b`

## References

The proof of associativity follows the note "Associativity of the Symmetric Difference of Sets: A
Proof from the Book" by John McCuan:

* <https://people.math.gatech.edu/~mccuan/courses/4317/symmetricdifference.pdf>

## Tags

boolean ring, generalized boolean algebra, boolean algebra, symmetric difference, bi-implication,
Heyting
-/

open Function OrderDual

variable {ι α β : Type*} {π : ι → Type*}

/-- The symmetric difference operator on a type with `⊔` and `\` is `(A \ B) ⊔ (B \ A)`. -/
def symmDiff [Max α] [SDiff α] (a b : α) : α :=
  a \ b ⊔ b \ a

/-- The Heyting bi-implication is `(b ⇨ a) ⊓ (a ⇨ b)`. This generalizes equivalence of
propositions. -/
def bihimp [Min α] [HImp α] (a b : α) : α :=
  (b ⇨ a) ⊓ (a ⇨ b)

/-- Notation for symmDiff -/
scoped[symmDiff] infixl:100 " ∆ " => symmDiff

/-- Notation for bihimp -/
scoped[symmDiff] infixl:100 " ⇔ " => bihimp

  rfl

  rfl

  rfl

* `symmDiff_comm`: commutative, and
* `symmDiff_assoc`: associative.

* `a ∆ b`: `symmDiff a b`
* `a ⇔ b`: `bihimp a b`

The proof of associativity follows the note "Associativity of the Symmetric Difference of Sets: A
Proof from the Book" by John McCuan:

/-!
# Symmetric difference and bi-implication

This file defines the symmetric difference and bi-implication operators in (co-)Heyting algebras.

## Examples

Some examples are
* The symmetric difference of two sets is the set of elements that are in either but not both.
* The symmetric difference on propositions is `Xor'`.
* The symmetric difference on `Bool` is `Bool.xor`.
* The equivalence of propositions. Two propositions are equivalent if they imply each other.
* The symmetric difference translates to addition when considering a Boolean algebra as a Boolean
  ring.

## Main declarations

* `symmDiff`: The symmetric difference operator, defined as `(a \ b) ⊔ (b \ a)`
* `bihimp`: The bi-implication operator, defined as `(b ⇨ a) ⊓ (a ⇨ b)`

In generalized Boolean algebras, the symmetric difference operator is:

* `symmDiff_comm`: commutative, and
* `symmDiff_assoc`: associative.

## Notations

* `a ∆ b`: `symmDiff a b`
* `a ⇔ b`: `bihimp a b`

## References

The proof of associativity follows the note "Associativity of the Symmetric Difference of Sets: A
Proof from the Book" by John McCuan:

* <https://people.math.gatech.edu/~mccuan/courses/4317/symmetricdifference.pdf>

## Tags

boolean ring, generalized boolean algebra, boolean algebra, symmetric difference, bi-implication,
Heyting
-/

/-- The symmetric difference operator on a type with `⊔` and `\` is `(A \ B) ⊔ (B \ A)`. -/
def symmDiff [Max α] [SDiff α] (a b : α) : α :=
  a \ b ⊔ b \ a

/-- The Heyting bi-implication is `(b ⇨ a) ⊓ (a ⇨ b)`. This generalizes equivalence of
propositions. -/
def bihimp [Min α] [HImp α] (a b : α) : α :=
  (b ⇨ a) ⊓ (a ⇨ b)

/-- Notation for bihimp -/
scoped[symmDiff] infixl:100 " ⇔ " => bihimp

/-!
# Symmetric difference and bi-implication

This file defines the symmetric difference and bi-implication operators in (co-)Heyting algebras.

## Examples

Some examples are
* The symmetric difference of two sets is the set of elements that are in either but not both.
* The symmetric difference on propositions is `Xor'`.
* The symmetric difference on `Bool` is `Bool.xor`.
* The equivalence of propositions. Two propositions are equivalent if they imply each other.
* The symmetric difference translates to addition when considering a Boolean algebra as a Boolean
  ring.

## Main declarations

* `symmDiff`: The symmetric difference operator, defined as `(a \ b) ⊔ (b \ a)`
* `bihimp`: The bi-implication operator, defined as `(b ⇨ a) ⊓ (a ⇨ b)`

In generalized Boolean algebras, the symmetric difference operator is:

* `symmDiff_comm`: commutative, and
* `symmDiff_assoc`: associative.

## Notations

* `a ∆ b`: `symmDiff a b`
* `a ⇔ b`: `bihimp a b`

## References

The proof of associativity follows the note "Associativity of the Symmetric Difference of Sets: A
Proof from the Book" by John McCuan:

* <https://people.math.gatech.edu/~mccuan/courses/4317/symmetricdifference.pdf>

## Tags

boolean ring, generalized boolean algebra, boolean algebra, symmetric difference, bi-implication,
Heyting
-/

variable {ι α β : Type*} {π : ι → Type*}

/-- The symmetric difference operator on a type with `⊔` and `\` is `(A \ B) ⊔ (B \ A)`. -/
def symmDiff [Max α] [SDiff α] (a b : α) : α :=
  a \ b ⊔ b \ a

/-- The Heyting bi-implication is `(b ⇨ a) ⊓ (a ⇨ b)`. This generalizes equivalence of
propositions. -/
def bihimp [Min α] [HImp α] (a b : α) : α :=
  (b ⇨ a) ⊓ (a ⇨ b)

/-- Notation for symmDiff -/

/-- Notation for bihimp -/
scoped[symmDiff] infixl:100 " ⇔ " => bihimp

  rfl

* `symmDiff_comm`: commutative, and
* `symmDiff_assoc`: associative.

* `a ∆ b`: `symmDiff a b`
* `a ⇔ b`: `bihimp a b`

The proof of associativity follows the note "Associativity of the Symmetric Difference of Sets: A
Proof from the Book" by John McCuan:

* <https://people.math.gatech.edu/~mccuan/courses/4317/symmetricdifference.pdf>

import Mathlib.Order.BooleanAlgebra

/-!
# Symmetric difference and bi-implication

This file defines the symmetric difference and bi-implication operators in (co-)Heyting algebras.

## Examples

Some examples are
* The symmetric difference of two sets is the set of elements that are in either but not both.
* The symmetric difference on propositions is `Xor'`.
* The symmetric difference on `Bool` is `Bool.xor`.
* The equivalence of propositions. Two propositions are equivalent if they imply each other.
* The symmetric difference translates to addition when considering a Boolean algebra as a Boolean
  ring.

## Main declarations

* `symmDiff`: The symmetric difference operator, defined as `(a \ b) ⊔ (b \ a)`
* `bihimp`: The bi-implication operator, defined as `(b ⇨ a) ⊓ (a ⇨ b)`

In generalized Boolean algebras, the symmetric difference operator is:

* `symmDiff_comm`: commutative, and
* `symmDiff_assoc`: associative.

## Notations

* `a ∆ b`: `symmDiff a b`
* `a ⇔ b`: `bihimp a b`

## References

The proof of associativity follows the note "Associativity of the Symmetric Difference of Sets: A
Proof from the Book" by John McCuan:

* <https://people.math.gatech.edu/~mccuan/courses/4317/symmetricdifference.pdf>

## Tags

boolean ring, generalized boolean algebra, boolean algebra, symmetric difference, bi-implication,
Heyting
-/

open Function OrderDual

variable {ι α β : Type*} {π : ι → Type*}

/-- The symmetric difference operator on a type with `⊔` and `\` is `(A \ B) ⊔ (B \ A)`. -/
def symmDiff [Max α] [SDiff α] (a b : α) : α :=
  a \ b ⊔ b \ a

/-- The Heyting bi-implication is `(b ⇨ a) ⊓ (a ⇨ b)`. This generalizes equivalence of
propositions. -/
def bihimp [Min α] [HImp α] (a b : α) : α :=
  (b ⇨ a) ⊓ (a ⇨ b)

/-- Notation for symmDiff -/
scoped[symmDiff] infixl:100 " ∆ " => symmDiff

/-- Notation for bihimp -/
scoped[symmDiff] infixl:100 " ⇔ " => bihimp

  rfl

theorem bihimp_def [Min α] [HImp α] (a b : α) : a ⇔ b = (b ⇨ a) ⊓ (a ⇨ b) :=
  rfl

  rfl

# Symmetric difference and bi-implication

This file defines the symmetric difference and bi-implication operators in (co-)Heyting algebras.

## Examples

Some examples are
* The symmetric difference of two sets is the set of elements that are in either but not both.
* The symmetric difference on propositions is `Xor'`.
* The symmetric difference on `Bool` is `Bool.xor`.
* The equivalence of propositions. Two propositions are equivalent if they imply each other.
* The symmetric difference translates to addition when considering a Boolean algebra as a Boolean
  ring.

## Main declarations

* `symmDiff`: The symmetric difference operator, defined as `(a \ b) ⊔ (b \ a)`
* `bihimp`: The bi-implication operator, defined as `(b ⇨ a) ⊓ (a ⇨ b)`

In generalized Boolean algebras, the symmetric difference operator is:

* `symmDiff_comm`: commutative, and
* `symmDiff_assoc`: associative.

## Notations

* `a ∆ b`: `symmDiff a b`
* `a ⇔ b`: `bihimp a b`

## References

The proof of associativity follows the note "Associativity of the Symmetric Difference of Sets: A
Proof from the Book" by John McCuan:

* <https://people.math.gatech.edu/~mccuan/courses/4317/symmetricdifference.pdf>

## Tags

Heyting
-/

propositions. -/

  · rw [sup_assoc]

/-!
# Symmetric difference and bi-implication

This file defines the symmetric difference and bi-implication operators in (co-)Heyting algebras.

## Examples

Some examples are
* The symmetric difference of two sets is the set of elements that are in either but not both.
* The symmetric difference on propositions is `Xor'`.
* The symmetric difference on `Bool` is `Bool.xor`.
* The equivalence of propositions. Two propositions are equivalent if they imply each other.
* The symmetric difference translates to addition when considering a Boolean algebra as a Boolean
  ring.

## Main declarations

* `symmDiff`: The symmetric difference operator, defined as `(a \ b) ⊔ (b \ a)`
* `bihimp`: The bi-implication operator, defined as `(b ⇨ a) ⊓ (a ⇨ b)`

In generalized Boolean algebras, the symmetric difference operator is:

* `symmDiff_comm`: commutative, and
* `symmDiff_assoc`: associative.

## Notations

* `a ∆ b`: `symmDiff a b`
* `a ⇔ b`: `bihimp a b`

## References

The proof of associativity follows the note "Associativity of the Symmetric Difference of Sets: A
Proof from the Book" by John McCuan:

* <https://people.math.gatech.edu/~mccuan/courses/4317/symmetricdifference.pdf>

## Tags

boolean ring, generalized boolean algebra, boolean algebra, symmetric difference, bi-implication,
Heyting
-/

/-- The symmetric difference operator on a type with `⊔` and `\` is `(A \ B) ⊔ (B \ A)`. -/

/-!
# Symmetric difference and bi-implication

This file defines the symmetric difference and bi-implication operators in (co-)Heyting algebras.

## Examples

Some examples are
* The symmetric difference of two sets is the set of elements that are in either but not both.
* The symmetric difference on propositions is `Xor'`.
* The symmetric difference on `Bool` is `Bool.xor`.
* The equivalence of propositions. Two propositions are equivalent if they imply each other.
* The symmetric difference translates to addition when considering a Boolean algebra as a Boolean
  ring.

## Main declarations

* `symmDiff`: The symmetric difference operator, defined as `(a \ b) ⊔ (b \ a)`
* `bihimp`: The bi-implication operator, defined as `(b ⇨ a) ⊓ (a ⇨ b)`

In generalized Boolean algebras, the symmetric difference operator is:

* `symmDiff_comm`: commutative, and
* `symmDiff_assoc`: associative.

## Notations

* `a ∆ b`: `symmDiff a b`
* `a ⇔ b`: `bihimp a b`

## References

The proof of associativity follows the note "Associativity of the Symmetric Difference of Sets: A
Proof from the Book" by John McCuan:

* <https://people.math.gatech.edu/~mccuan/courses/4317/symmetricdifference.pdf>

## Tags

Heyting
-/

variable {ι α β : Type*} {π : ι → Type*}

/-- The symmetric difference operator on a type with `⊔` and `\` is `(A \ B) ⊔ (B \ A)`. -/
def symmDiff [Max α] [SDiff α] (a b : α) : α :=
  a \ b ⊔ b \ a

/-- The Heyting bi-implication is `(b ⇨ a) ⊓ (a ⇨ b)`. This generalizes equivalence of
propositions. -/
def bihimp [Min α] [HImp α] (a b : α) : α :=
  (b ⇨ a) ⊓ (a ⇨ b)

/-- Notation for symmDiff -/
scoped[symmDiff] infixl:100 " ∆ " => symmDiff

/-- Notation for bihimp -/
scoped[symmDiff] infixl:100 " ⇔ " => bihimp

theorem symmDiff_def [Max α] [SDiff α] (a b : α) : a ∆ b = a \ b ⊔ b \ a :=
  rfl

theorem bihimp_def [Min α] [HImp α] (a b : α) : a ⇔ b = (b ⇨ a) ⊓ (a ⇨ b) :=
  rfl

theorem symmDiff_eq_Xor' (p q : Prop) : p ∆ q = Xor' p q :=
  rfl

@[simp]
theorem bihimp_iff_iff {p q : Prop} : p ⇔ q ↔ (p ↔ q) :=
  iff_iff_implies_and_implies.symm.trans Iff.comm

theorem Bool.symmDiff_eq_xor : ∀ p q : Bool, p ∆ q = xor p q := by decide

  rw [symmDiff, sdiff_eq_bot_iff.2 h, sup_bot_eq]

  simp_rw [symmDiff, sup_le_iff, sdiff_le_iff]

  exact

      (sup_le le_sdiff_sup <| le_sdiff_sup.trans <| sup_le le_sup_right le_sdiff_sup)

  rw [symmDiff_comm, symmDiff_sdiff_eq_sup, sup_comm]

  refine le_antisymm (sup_le symmDiff_le_sup inf_le_sup) ?_
  rw [sup_inf_left, symmDiff]
  refine sup_le (le_inf le_sup_right ?_) (le_inf ?_ le_sup_right)
  · rw [sup_right_comm]
    exact le_sup_of_le_left le_sdiff_sup
  · rw [sup_assoc]
    exact le_sup_of_le_right le_sdiff_sup

  rw [← symmDiff_sdiff_inf a, sdiff_symmDiff_eq_sup, symmDiff_sup_inf]

theorem inf_symmDiff_symmDiff : (a ⊓ b) ∆ (a ∆ b) = a ⊔ b := by
  rw [symmDiff_comm, symmDiff_symmDiff_inf]

  refine (sup_le_sup (sdiff_triangle a b c) <| sdiff_triangle _ b _).trans_eq ?_
  rw [sup_comm (c \ b), sup_sup_sup_comm, symmDiff, symmDiff]

  convert symmDiff_triangle a b ⊥ <;> rw [symmDiff_bot]

theorem le_symmDiff_sup_left (a b : α) : b ≤ (a ∆ b) ⊔ a :=
  symmDiff_comm a b ▸ le_symmDiff_sup_right ..

# Symmetric difference and bi-implication

This file defines the symmetric difference and bi-implication operators in (co-)Heyting algebras.

## Examples

Some examples are
* The symmetric difference of two sets is the set of elements that are in either but not both.
* The symmetric difference on propositions is `Xor'`.
* The symmetric difference on `Bool` is `Bool.xor`.
* The equivalence of propositions. Two propositions are equivalent if they imply each other.
* The symmetric difference translates to addition when considering a Boolean algebra as a Boolean
  ring.

## Main declarations

* `symmDiff`: The symmetric difference operator, defined as `(a \ b) ⊔ (b \ a)`
* `bihimp`: The bi-implication operator, defined as `(b ⇨ a) ⊓ (a ⇨ b)`

In generalized Boolean algebras, the symmetric difference operator is:

* `symmDiff_comm`: commutative, and
* `symmDiff_assoc`: associative.

## Notations

* `a ∆ b`: `symmDiff a b`
* `a ⇔ b`: `bihimp a b`

## References

The proof of associativity follows the note "Associativity of the Symmetric Difference of Sets: A
Proof from the Book" by John McCuan:

* <https://people.math.gatech.edu/~mccuan/courses/4317/symmetricdifference.pdf>

## Tags

Heyting
-/

/-- The symmetric difference operator on a type with `⊔` and `\` is `(A \ B) ⊔ (B \ A)`. -/

  a \ b ⊔ b \ a

/-- The Heyting bi-implication is `(b ⇨ a) ⊓ (a ⇨ b)`. This generalizes equivalence of
propositions. -/
def bihimp [Min α] [HImp α] (a b : α) : α :=
  (b ⇨ a) ⊓ (a ⇨ b)

/-!
# Symmetric difference and bi-implication

This file defines the symmetric difference and bi-implication operators in (co-)Heyting algebras.

## Examples

Some examples are
* The symmetric difference of two sets is the set of elements that are in either but not both.
* The symmetric difference on propositions is `Xor'`.
* The symmetric difference on `Bool` is `Bool.xor`.
* The equivalence of propositions. Two propositions are equivalent if they imply each other.
* The symmetric difference translates to addition when considering a Boolean algebra as a Boolean
  ring.

## Main declarations

* `symmDiff`: The symmetric difference operator, defined as `(a \ b) ⊔ (b \ a)`
* `bihimp`: The bi-implication operator, defined as `(b ⇨ a) ⊓ (a ⇨ b)`

In generalized Boolean algebras, the symmetric difference operator is:

* `symmDiff_comm`: commutative, and
* `symmDiff_assoc`: associative.

## Notations

* `a ∆ b`: `symmDiff a b`
* `a ⇔ b`: `bihimp a b`

## References

The proof of associativity follows the note "Associativity of the Symmetric Difference of Sets: A
Proof from the Book" by John McCuan:

* <https://people.math.gatech.edu/~mccuan/courses/4317/symmetricdifference.pdf>

## Tags

boolean ring, generalized boolean algebra, boolean algebra, symmetric difference, bi-implication,
Heyting
-/

This file defines the symmetric difference and bi-implication operators in (co-)Heyting algebras.

## Examples

Some examples are
* The symmetric difference of two sets is the set of elements that are in either but not both.
* The symmetric difference on propositions is `Xor'`.
* The symmetric difference on `Bool` is `Bool.xor`.
* The equivalence of propositions. Two propositions are equivalent if they imply each other.
* The symmetric difference translates to addition when considering a Boolean algebra as a Boolean
  ring.

## Main declarations

* `symmDiff`: The symmetric difference operator, defined as `(a \ b) ⊔ (b \ a)`
* `bihimp`: The bi-implication operator, defined as `(b ⇨ a) ⊓ (a ⇨ b)`

In generalized Boolean algebras, the symmetric difference operator is:

* `symmDiff_comm`: commutative, and
* `symmDiff_assoc`: associative.

## Notations

* `a ∆ b`: `symmDiff a b`
* `a ⇔ b`: `bihimp a b`

## References

The proof of associativity follows the note "Associativity of the Symmetric Difference of Sets: A
Proof from the Book" by John McCuan:

* <https://people.math.gatech.edu/~mccuan/courses/4317/symmetricdifference.pdf>

Heyting
-/

This file defines the symmetric difference and bi-implication operators in (co-)Heyting algebras.

## Examples

Some examples are
* The symmetric difference of two sets is the set of elements that are in either but not both.
* The symmetric difference on propositions is `Xor'`.
* The symmetric difference on `Bool` is `Bool.xor`.
* The equivalence of propositions. Two propositions are equivalent if they imply each other.

  ring.

* `symmDiff`: The symmetric difference operator, defined as `(a \ b) ⊔ (b \ a)`
* `bihimp`: The bi-implication operator, defined as `(b ⇨ a) ⊓ (a ⇨ b)`

In generalized Boolean algebras, the symmetric difference operator is:

* `symmDiff_comm`: commutative, and
* `symmDiff_assoc`: associative.

## Notations

* `a ∆ b`: `symmDiff a b`
* `a ⇔ b`: `bihimp a b`

## References

The proof of associativity follows the note "Associativity of the Symmetric Difference of Sets: A
Proof from the Book" by John McCuan:

* <https://people.math.gatech.edu/~mccuan/courses/4317/symmetricdifference.pdf>

Heyting
-/

* The symmetric difference of two sets is the set of elements that are in either but not both.

* `symmDiff_comm`: commutative, and
* `symmDiff_assoc`: associative.

## Notations

* `a ∆ b`: `symmDiff a b`
* `a ⇔ b`: `bihimp a b`

## References

The proof of associativity follows the note "Associativity of the Symmetric Difference of Sets: A
Proof from the Book" by John McCuan:

* <https://people.math.gatech.edu/~mccuan/courses/4317/symmetricdifference.pdf>

Heyting

import Mathlib.Logic.Equiv.Basic

/-!
# Symmetric difference and bi-implication

This file defines the symmetric difference and bi-implication operators in (co-)Heyting algebras.

## Examples

Some examples are
* The symmetric difference of two sets is the set of elements that are in either but not both.
* The symmetric difference on propositions is `Xor'`.
* The symmetric difference on `Bool` is `Bool.xor`.
* The equivalence of propositions. Two propositions are equivalent if they imply each other.
* The symmetric difference translates to addition when considering a Boolean algebra as a Boolean
  ring.

## Main declarations

* `symmDiff`: The symmetric difference operator, defined as `(a \ b) ⊔ (b \ a)`
* `bihimp`: The bi-implication operator, defined as `(b ⇨ a) ⊓ (a ⇨ b)`

In generalized Boolean algebras, the symmetric difference operator is:

* `symmDiff_comm`: commutative, and
* `symmDiff_assoc`: associative.

## Notations

* `a ∆ b`: `symmDiff a b`
* `a ⇔ b`: `bihimp a b`

## References

The proof of associativity follows the note "Associativity of the Symmetric Difference of Sets: A
Proof from the Book" by John McCuan:

* <https://people.math.gatech.edu/~mccuan/courses/4317/symmetricdifference.pdf>

## Tags

boolean ring, generalized boolean algebra, boolean algebra, symmetric difference, bi-implication,
Heyting
-/

assert_not_exists RelIso

open Function OrderDual

variable {ι α β : Type*} {π : ι → Type*}

/-- The symmetric difference operator on a type with `⊔` and `\` is `(A \ B) ⊔ (B \ A)`. -/
def symmDiff [Max α] [SDiff α] (a b : α) : α :=
  a \ b ⊔ b \ a

/-- The Heyting bi-implication is `(b ⇨ a) ⊓ (a ⇨ b)`. This generalizes equivalence of
propositions. -/
def bihimp [Min α] [HImp α] (a b : α) : α :=
  (b ⇨ a) ⊓ (a ⇨ b)

/-- Notation for symmDiff -/
scoped[symmDiff] infixl:100 " ∆ " => symmDiff

/-- Notation for bihimp -/
scoped[symmDiff] infixl:100 " ⇔ " => bihimp

open scoped symmDiff

theorem symmDiff_def [Max α] [SDiff α] (a b : α) : a ∆ b = a \ b ⊔ b \ a :=
  rfl

theorem bihimp_def [Min α] [HImp α] (a b : α) : a ⇔ b = (b ⇨ a) ⊓ (a ⇨ b) :=
  rfl

theorem symmDiff_eq_Xor' (p q : Prop) : p ∆ q = Xor' p q :=
  rfl

@[simp]
theorem bihimp_iff_iff {p q : Prop} : p ⇔ q ↔ (p ↔ q) :=
  iff_iff_implies_and_implies.symm.trans Iff.comm

@[simp]
theorem Bool.symmDiff_eq_xor : ∀ p q : Bool, p ∆ q = xor p q := by decide

section GeneralizedCoheytingAlgebra

variable [GeneralizedCoheytingAlgebra α] (a b c : α)

@[simp]
theorem toDual_symmDiff : toDual (a ∆ b) = toDual a ⇔ toDual b :=
  rfl

@[simp]
theorem ofDual_bihimp (a b : αᵒᵈ) : ofDual (a ⇔ b) = ofDual a ∆ ofDual b :=
  rfl

theorem symmDiff_comm : a ∆ b = b ∆ a := by simp only [symmDiff, sup_comm]

instance symmDiff_isCommutative : Std.Commutative (α := α) (· ∆ ·) :=
  ⟨symmDiff_comm⟩

@[simp]
theorem symmDiff_self : a ∆ a = ⊥ := by rw [symmDiff, sup_idem, sdiff_self]

@[simp]
theorem symmDiff_bot : a ∆ ⊥ = a := by rw [symmDiff, sdiff_bot, bot_sdiff, sup_bot_eq]

@[simp]
theorem bot_symmDiff : ⊥ ∆ a = a := by rw [symmDiff_comm, symmDiff_bot]

@[simp]
theorem symmDiff_eq_bot {a b : α} : a ∆ b = ⊥ ↔ a = b := by
  simp_rw [symmDiff, sup_eq_bot_iff, sdiff_eq_bot_iff, le_antisymm_iff]

theorem symmDiff_of_le {a b : α} (h : a ≤ b) : a ∆ b = b \ a := by
  rw [symmDiff, sdiff_eq_bot_iff.2 h, bot_sup_eq]

theorem symmDiff_of_ge {a b : α} (h : b ≤ a) : a ∆ b = a \ b := by
  rw [symmDiff, sdiff_eq_bot_iff.2 h, sup_bot_eq]

theorem symmDiff_le {a b c : α} (ha : a ≤ b ⊔ c) (hb : b ≤ a ⊔ c) : a ∆ b ≤ c :=
  sup_le (sdiff_le_iff.2 ha) <| sdiff_le_iff.2 hb

theorem symmDiff_le_iff {a b c : α} : a ∆ b ≤ c ↔ a ≤ b ⊔ c ∧ b ≤ a ⊔ c := by
  simp_rw [symmDiff, sup_le_iff, sdiff_le_iff]

@[simp]
theorem symmDiff_le_sup {a b : α} : a ∆ b ≤ a ⊔ b :=
  sup_le_sup sdiff_le sdiff_le

theorem symmDiff_eq_sup_sdiff_inf : a ∆ b = (a ⊔ b) \ (a ⊓ b) := by simp [sup_sdiff, symmDiff]

theorem Disjoint.symmDiff_eq_sup {a b : α} (h : Disjoint a b) : a ∆ b = a ⊔ b := by
  rw [symmDiff, h.sdiff_eq_left, h.sdiff_eq_right]

theorem symmDiff_sdiff : a ∆ b \ c = a \ (b ⊔ c) ⊔ b \ (a ⊔ c) := by
  rw [symmDiff, sup_sdiff_distrib, sdiff_sdiff_left, sdiff_sdiff_left]

@[simp]
theorem symmDiff_sdiff_inf : a ∆ b \ (a ⊓ b) = a ∆ b := by
  rw [symmDiff_sdiff]
  simp [symmDiff]

@[simp]
theorem symmDiff_sdiff_eq_sup : a ∆ (b \ a) = a ⊔ b := by
  rw [symmDiff, sdiff_idem]
  exact
    le_antisymm (sup_le_sup sdiff_le sdiff_le)
      (sup_le le_sdiff_sup <| le_sdiff_sup.trans <| sup_le le_sup_right le_sdiff_sup)

@[simp]
theorem sdiff_symmDiff_eq_sup : (a \ b) ∆ b = a ⊔ b := by
  rw [symmDiff_comm, symmDiff_sdiff_eq_sup, sup_comm]

@[simp]
theorem symmDiff_sup_inf : a ∆ b ⊔ a ⊓ b = a ⊔ b := by
  refine le_antisymm (sup_le symmDiff_le_sup inf_le_sup) ?_
  rw [sup_inf_left, symmDiff]
  refine sup_le (le_inf le_sup_right ?_) (le_inf ?_ le_sup_right)
  · rw [sup_right_comm]
    exact le_sup_of_le_left le_sdiff_sup
  · rw [sup_assoc]
    exact le_sup_of_le_right le_sdiff_sup

@[simp]
theorem inf_sup_symmDiff : a ⊓ b ⊔ a ∆ b = a ⊔ b := by rw [sup_comm, symmDiff_sup_inf]

@[simp]
theorem symmDiff_symmDiff_inf : a ∆ b ∆ (a ⊓ b) = a ⊔ b := by
  rw [← symmDiff_sdiff_inf a, sdiff_symmDiff_eq_sup, symmDiff_sup_inf]

@[simp]
theorem inf_symmDiff_symmDiff : (a ⊓ b) ∆ (a ∆ b) = a ⊔ b := by
  rw [symmDiff_comm, symmDiff_symmDiff_inf]

theorem symmDiff_triangle : a ∆ c ≤ a ∆ b ⊔ b ∆ c := by
  refine (sup_le_sup (sdiff_triangle a b c) <| sdiff_triangle _ b _).trans_eq ?_
  rw [sup_comm (c \ b), sup_sup_sup_comm, symmDiff, symmDiff]

theorem le_symmDiff_sup_right (a b : α) : a ≤ (a ∆ b) ⊔ b := by
  convert symmDiff_triangle a b ⊥ <;> rw [symmDiff_bot]

theorem le_symmDiff_sup_left (a b : α) : b ≤ (a ∆ b) ⊔ a :=
  symmDiff_comm a b ▸ le_symmDiff_sup_right ..

end GeneralizedCoheytingAlgebra

* `symmDiff_assoc`: associative.

* `a ∆ b`: `symmDiff a b`
* `a ⇔ b`: `bihimp a b`

The proof of associativity follows the note "Associativity of the Symmetric Difference of Sets: A
Proof from the Book" by John McCuan:

* <https://people.math.gatech.edu/~mccuan/courses/4317/symmetricdifference.pdf>

* The symmetric difference of two sets is the set of elements that are in either but not both.

* `symmDiff_assoc`: associative.

* `a ∆ b`: `symmDiff a b`
* `a ⇔ b`: `bihimp a b`

The proof of associativity follows the note "Associativity of the Symmetric Difference of Sets: A
Proof from the Book" by John McCuan:

* <https://people.math.gatech.edu/~mccuan/courses/4317/symmetricdifference.pdf>

Heyting
-/

## Examples

Some examples are
* The symmetric difference of two sets is the set of elements that are in either but not both.
* The symmetric difference on propositions is `Xor'`.
* The symmetric difference on `Bool` is `Bool.xor`.
* The equivalence of propositions. Two propositions are equivalent if they imply each other.
* The symmetric difference translates to addition when considering a Boolean algebra as a Boolean
  ring.

## Main declarations

* `symmDiff`: The symmetric difference operator, defined as `(a \ b) ⊔ (b \ a)`
* `bihimp`: The bi-implication operator, defined as `(b ⇨ a) ⊓ (a ⇨ b)`

In generalized Boolean algebras, the symmetric difference operator is:

* `symmDiff_comm`: commutative, and
* `symmDiff_assoc`: associative.

## Notations

* `a ∆ b`: `symmDiff a b`
* `a ⇔ b`: `bihimp a b`

## References

The proof of associativity follows the note "Associativity of the Symmetric Difference of Sets: A
Proof from the Book" by John McCuan:

* <https://people.math.gatech.edu/~mccuan/courses/4317/symmetricdifference.pdf>

## Tags

Heyting
-/

open Function OrderDual

variable {ι α β : Type*} {π : ι → Type*}

/-- The symmetric difference operator on a type with `⊔` and `\` is `(A \ B) ⊔ (B \ A)`. -/
def symmDiff [Max α] [SDiff α] (a b : α) : α :=
  a \ b ⊔ b \ a

/-- The Heyting bi-implication is `(b ⇨ a) ⊓ (a ⇨ b)`. This generalizes equivalence of
propositions. -/
def bihimp [Min α] [HImp α] (a b : α) : α :=
  (b ⇨ a) ⊓ (a ⇨ b)

/-- Notation for symmDiff -/
scoped[symmDiff] infixl:100 " ∆ " => symmDiff

/-- Notation for bihimp -/
scoped[symmDiff] infixl:100 " ⇔ " => bihimp

open scoped symmDiff

theorem symmDiff_def [Max α] [SDiff α] (a b : α) : a ∆ b = a \ b ⊔ b \ a :=
  rfl

theorem bihimp_def [Min α] [HImp α] (a b : α) : a ⇔ b = (b ⇨ a) ⊓ (a ⇨ b) :=
  rfl

theorem symmDiff_eq_Xor' (p q : Prop) : p ∆ q = Xor' p q :=
  rfl

@[simp]
theorem bihimp_iff_iff {p q : Prop} : p ⇔ q ↔ (p ↔ q) :=
  iff_iff_implies_and_implies.symm.trans Iff.comm

@[simp]
theorem Bool.symmDiff_eq_xor : ∀ p q : Bool, p ∆ q = xor p q := by decide

variable [GeneralizedCoheytingAlgebra α] (a b c : α)

@[simp]
theorem toDual_symmDiff : toDual (a ∆ b) = toDual a ⇔ toDual b :=
  rfl

@[simp]
theorem ofDual_bihimp (a b : αᵒᵈ) : ofDual (a ⇔ b) = ofDual a ∆ ofDual b :=
  rfl

theorem symmDiff_comm : a ∆ b = b ∆ a := by simp only [symmDiff, sup_comm]

instance symmDiff_isCommutative : Std.Commutative (α := α) (· ∆ ·) :=
  ⟨symmDiff_comm⟩

@[simp]

@[simp]

@[simp]
theorem symmDiff_eq_bot {a b : α} : a ∆ b = ⊥ ↔ a = b := by
  simp_rw [symmDiff, sup_eq_bot_iff, sdiff_eq_bot_iff, le_antisymm_iff]

  rw [symmDiff, sdiff_eq_bot_iff.2 h, bot_sup_eq]

theorem symmDiff_of_ge {a b : α} (h : b ≤ a) : a ∆ b = a \ b := by
  rw [symmDiff, sdiff_eq_bot_iff.2 h, sup_bot_eq]

theorem symmDiff_le {a b c : α} (ha : a ≤ b ⊔ c) (hb : b ≤ a ⊔ c) : a ∆ b ≤ c :=
  sup_le (sdiff_le_iff.2 ha) <| sdiff_le_iff.2 hb

theorem symmDiff_le_iff {a b c : α} : a ∆ b ≤ c ↔ a ≤ b ⊔ c ∧ b ≤ a ⊔ c := by
  simp_rw [symmDiff, sup_le_iff, sdiff_le_iff]

  sup_le_sup sdiff_le sdiff_le

  rw [symmDiff, sup_sdiff_distrib, sdiff_sdiff_left, sdiff_sdiff_left]
